body.input: Let's start with the big historical question. How have computers changed in

body.input: the past 50 years at both the fundamental architectural level and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: in general, in your eyes? Well, the biggest thing that happened was the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: invention of the microprocessor. So computers that used to fill up

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: several rooms could fit inside your cell phone.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: And not only did they get smaller, they got a lot faster. So they're

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: a million times faster than they were 50 years ago

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: and they're much cheaper and they're ubiquitous.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: There's 7.8 billion people on this planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: Probably half of them have cell phones right now, just remarkable.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: There's probably more microprocessors than there are people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: Sure, I don't know what the ratio is, but I'm sure it's above one.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: Maybe it's 10 to 1 or some number like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: What is a microprocessor? So a way to say what a microprocessor is, is to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: tell you what's inside a computer. So a computer forever has classically had

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: five pieces. There's input and output, which kind of naturally,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: as you'd expect, is input is like speech or typing and output is displays.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: There's a memory and like the name sounds, it remembers things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: So it's integrated circuits whose job is you put information in them. When you

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: ask for it, it comes back out. That's memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: And the third part is the processor, where the team

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: microprocessor comes from. And that has two pieces

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: as well, and that is the control, which is kind of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: of the processor and what's called the arithmetic unit. It's kind of the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: brawn of the computer. So if you think of the as a human body, the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: arithmetic unit, the thing that does the number crunching is the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: is the body and the control is the brain. So those five pieces,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: input, output, memory, arithmetic unit and control have been

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: computers since the very dawn. And the last two are considered the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

body.input: processor. So a microprocessor simply means a processor that fits on a

metadata.title: Podcast: David Patterson: Computer Architecture and Data Storage | Lex Fridman Podcast #104

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: part of the future of Ethereum.

body.input: Let's not call it Ethereum 2.0,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but the future of Ethereum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: That also may require a hard fork,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I don't know if you can correct me on this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is well, broadly, ideas for scaling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And more specifically sort of layer two

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: or layer one and two intersection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: ideas of how to achieve scaling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And at the core of that is the idea of sharding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So first, what is sharding?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So there's two major paradigms for scaling blockchains,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: right, as you said, layer one and layer two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And layer one basically means make the blockchain itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: capable of processing more transactions

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: by having some mechanism by which you can do that

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: despite the fact that there's a limit to the capacity

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of each participant in the blockchain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then layer two says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: well, we're gonna keep the blockchain as is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but we're gonna create clever protocols

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that sit on top of the blockchain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that still use the blockchain

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and then still kind of inherit things

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like the security guarantees of a blockchain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But at the same time, a lot of things are done off chain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and so you get more scalability that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So in Ethereum, the most popular paradigm

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for layer two is rollups,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and the most popular paradigm for layer one is sharding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So one way to achieve layer one scaling

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So maybe you can also comment on where,

body.input: and the very basic aspect before we even get to sharding

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So the way that I think about the trade-off

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is I think about it as a trade-off

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: between making it easy to write to the blockchain

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and making it easy to read the blockchain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So when I say read, I just mean have a node

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and actually verify it and make sure that it's correct

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and all of those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then by write, I mean send transactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So I think for decentralization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: it's important for both of these tasks to be accessible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And I think that they're about equally importance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: If you have a chain that's too expensive to read,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then everyone will just trust a few people to read for them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then those people can change the rules

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: without anyone else's permission.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But if on the other hand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: it becomes really expensive to write,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then everyone will move on to basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: second layer systems that are incredibly centralized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And that takes away from decentralization

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and self-sovereignty as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So this has been my viewpoints

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: pretty much the whole time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It's that you need this balance

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and going in one direction or the other direction

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is very unhealthy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: basically what happened was that Bitcoin originally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: at the very beginning, it didn't really have a block size.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It just had an accidental block size of 32 meg,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: or block size limit of 32 megabytes

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: because that just happens to be the limit

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of the peer-to-peer messages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But then-

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Interesting, I didn't even know that part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yeah, but then Satoshi back in 2010

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And I think the-

body.input: By put, you mean sneaked in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yeah, just like made an update to the Bitcoin software

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that made blocks bigger than one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think it's a million bytes invalid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And I think the impression that most people had at the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is that this is just a temporary safety measure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And over time, as we become more confident in the software,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that limit would be raised somewhat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But then when the actual usage of the blockchain

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: started going up, and then it started going up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: first to 100 kilobytes per block,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then to 250 kilobytes per block,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then to 500 kilobytes per block,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: there started coming out of the woodworks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: this opinion that no, that limit should just not be increased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then there are all of these attempts at compromising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: First there was a proposal for 20 megabyte blocks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then there was the 248 proposal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: which is a bit ironic because the 248 proposal

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: started off being a small block negotiating position.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But then when the big block people came back and said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like, hey, aren't we gonna do this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: They're like, oh, no, no, no,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: we don't want the block size increases anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So there were these two different positions, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: The small blockers, I think they valued

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: one megabyte blocks for two reasons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: One is that they just like really, really believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in the importance of being able to read the chain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But two is that a lot of them really believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in maintaining this norm of never hard forking, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So the difference between a hard fork and a soft fork

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is basically that in a soft fork,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: any block that's valid under the new rules

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: was still valid under the old rules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So if you have a client that verifies

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: according to the old rules,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then you'll still be able to accept the chain

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that follows the new rules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Whereas with a hard fork, like you have to update your code

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in order to stay on the chain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And look, they have this belief that soft forks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: are kind of either less coercive than hard forks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: which by the way, I completely disagree with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I actually think soft forks are more coercive

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: because basically they force everyone who disagrees

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to sort of go along by default.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Or they have this opinion that it's more difficult

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to abuse soft forks to do really mean things

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: or that completely violate people's expectations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like increasing the supply, which is again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think there is some truth to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So because of these reasons, they just say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: we're only going to do soft forks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and we want to just not do any hard forks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And they eventually discovered this idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: called segregated witness that allows

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for like a very tiny block size increase

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to like the equivalent of about two megabytes

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: with a soft fork.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It's this really like weird and devious trick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like basically what they do is they take the signatures

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of transactions and then they put them outside of the block.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then they add an extra rule that says that like every,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for a block to be valid, the block has to come

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: with a separate like basically extension block

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that contains all of the transaction signatures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So when you measure it, according to the old rules,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like, no, hey, it adds up to less than a million,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but actually there's this extension block

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that the old protocol doesn't even know about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So-

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It's a hack that seemed to work to do in a small way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: extend the size of the block size.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So, small block side was like happy

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: with these very low levels of block size.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then the big block side wanted to expand to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: at the very least go to four megabytes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then maybe go maybe eight to 20.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There are those disagreements within there as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I definitely was favoring the big side

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: the whole way through as you can probably tell, but-

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Even though, so the argument against the big

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is that it makes things more centralized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yes, because fewer people can run a node

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: would require a hard fork and hard forks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Well, let's, okay, I think that's a beautiful principle

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and the people on the ETC side split off,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think it also just happens that a lot of the people

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that were not willing to stomach the Dow fork

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and then join the ETC side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: they were the more Bitcoin-y types

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and the more Bitcoin-y types do also tend to

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like proof of work more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so like that also sort of ended up, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: sort of like purifying the communities on both sides, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So Ethereum Classic is not switching to proof of stake

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and, you know, they're happy with their setup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And by the time that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: it came to the Beacon Chain launching

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and now I think the community is very strongly

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in favor of the proof of stake switch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But let me ask the question that no engineer wants to hear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: which is the question of timeline.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: When do you think the merge will happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Do you have a sense it might happen this year?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Do you have a sense it might be pushed

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: towards next year, 2022 or even beyond?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think early 2022 is the most realistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There's nothing, there's definitely still

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like an optimistic case of it happening this year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but the realistic thing to count on

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is definitely the early part of next year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Is there specific things that stand out to you there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like, do they'll make you feel good about progress

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: if you see it happening?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So the thing that we had last month

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is we had this online hackathon called Rayonism

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: where basically a bunch of the different client developers

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that are going to be part of the transition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like hacks together some test nets

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of the post-merge Ethereum chain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So these were only test nets

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of what would happen after the merge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: They were not test nets of the transition itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So the thing that people are working on now actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is the transition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So having a full specification

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of both the transition and post-transition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and we have specifications now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but in a realistic way, they'll probably needs

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to have a couple of changes and have things

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that continue to be ironed out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and then have a test net that does both the transition

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and the post-transition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then once you have a test network,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then you just have to do a lot of testing and audit it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and then do some runs on not just a specialized test network,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but on say an existing test network

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like a ROPS and a Rinkabee

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that Ethereum people already significantly use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And if it works,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then you can deploy the transition on main net.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Just as a quick comment, because this is fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: In August of last year, there was this Medalla.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I believe it's pronounced Medasha.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It's a South American subway station, I forget where.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But spelled with two L's.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yeah, yeah, because that's how Spanish works, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like the two L's have a.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Medasha.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yeah. Okay, cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Anyway, but I read about it in middle of August, August 14th,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: there was an incident on that test net.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: How does this process work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like what do you learn from those kinds of incidents

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: when stuff goes wrong in the test process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think that incident was that

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: there was a consensus failure of some kind, as I remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like basically just different clients

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: interpreting things in different ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and then one of them getting kicked off the network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then it ended up taking a while to actually like

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: get everyone to get back online.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like a big part of the reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: why it took weeks to resolve right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Is because it's on a test network,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like the coins are valueless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so there's not really this big push of any kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for people to actually go and download a new client

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: so they can start participating again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so it definitely took a while

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: until the chain started finalizing again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But, and then also like there was, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: another round of just not finalizing in October,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: as I remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There were definitely things that we learned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like there were a lot of things, especially,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that client developers just learned about optimization

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and how to build their clients

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in a way that they can process things efficiently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There's a lot that we learned

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: from just like seeing the full life cycle

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of what happens when more than a third of the validators

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: go offline and then finalization stops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then that kind of weird, unusual state

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of the chain continues for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then eventually everyone who was not participating

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: just gets enough of their stake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like we don't use the word slash,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: we use the word leaked for this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but like basically also burned until, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: the people who are participating go back up to two thirds

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and then the chain goes back to finalizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So just seeing all of those edge cases play out live,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think actually helped a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and probably helped to really contribute

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to making us feel better about Mainnet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I mean, there's also an incident just recently

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in April 24th of 2021,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: where this was on Beacon, I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There was a bug discovered in the software client Prism

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that prevented roughly 70% of validators

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: on the network from producing blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I mean, maybe you can comment on what happened,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but broadly, like the big picture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: what kind of stuff are you worried about

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in terms of problems that might arise?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: We're talking about small bugs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: are we talking about like emergent social, unexpected,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: social bugs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: You know, what are the things that worry you about

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: the future of Ethereum that you want to make sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: you construct mechanisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that prevent those things from happening?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So one of the lucky things there was

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that this particular bug only prevented proposals of blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It did not prevent attestations, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So attestations is just a mechanism for voting on blocks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and it's the attestations that are actually responsible

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for the chain finalizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So like coming to this more permanent agreements on blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So the chain was actually quite stable all the way through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: I think the thing that we generally learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: from these experiences is just how valuable it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to have this multi-client network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So this is one of these areas

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: where I think Ethereum distinguishes itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: from like Bitcoin, for example, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: That in Ethereum, we don't have one single client

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that everyone just runs, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There's multiple implementations of the protocol.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And these multiple implementations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: they all process and verify the blocks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that each other can verify, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So they all speak the same language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Now, sometimes when there's a bug, they disagree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And when two clients disagree because of a bug,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: we call this a consensus failure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And consensus failures are pretty serious, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And when you have a client's monoculture

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like Bitcoin does, then it's more rare

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to have consensus failures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Though you still have them actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Bitcoin had a consensus failure

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: between two different versions of the same client

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: back in 2013, but they're less likely to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But the interesting thing is that the multi-client

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: architecture has actually, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: saved Ethereum much more than it's hurt it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So even in this most recent incident, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like Prism was not producing blocks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but all the other clients were still producing blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There's four others, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yes, it's Prism, Nimbus, Teku, and the Lighthouse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then also Ethereum back in 2016

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: had this fun event that we call the Shanghai DOS attacks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: They're called that because the attacks started

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: right on the first day of our annual conference,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: DEF CON, that happens to be in Shanghai that year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So what happened basically was that someone came up

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: with a way to create blocks that were very slow

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for one client to process, but not the other client.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So at that time, there were basically two Ethereum clients.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: They were called Geth and Parity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Right now, I think the top three ones are Geth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Nethermind, and Beisu.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But what happened as a result of us having two clients

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is that the attacker was just not able to come up

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: with blocks that both clients were completely failing

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: at processing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so a lot of the miners and a lot of network participants,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: they just kept on switching between the two implementations

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: depending on which one worked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And that actually really helped the chain

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: survive through that month of attacks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: as the attacker just kept on hammering at our system

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and identifying all of the weaknesses

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and just forcing our clients to do this rapid sprint

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: of just optimizing the hell out of everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and make sure there aren't any of those DOS blocks

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: or DOS bugs remaining.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So that was another example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then as a counter example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: so something that also shows the point from the other side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Bitcoin had this bug in 2010, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: The balance overflow bug.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Basically someone created a transaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that had two outputs and those outputs

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: were both of a few billion Bitcoin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So about two to the power of 63 satoshis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then if you add those numbers together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: you go above two to the power of 64.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And of course, computers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: once you go above two to the power of 64, you wrap around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so the Bitcoin nodes thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that there was enough money to pay for the transaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: because it was asking for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: let's say like a billion satoshis or something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but actually it was asking for

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: two to the power of 64 plus a billion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so the attacker just managed to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like billions of Bitcoin out of thin air.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And this was not only discovered and fixed

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: after something like 12 hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: But if Bitcoin had been a multiple implementation system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: then what would have almost certainly happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is like one of the clients would have bugged out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but the other clients would have probably

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: actually had to check for that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so there would have been a consensus failure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but at least that would have like alerted everyone

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that there is a problem very quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And it also would have given everyone

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: just like obvious social permission to go and,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: pick whichever one of the chains is correct

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and solve the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So like that's, I think a big learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that we've had from multiple of our experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: in the Ethereum ecosystem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: just like validating this multi-client model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And to be fair, it's a model

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that we get criticized for a lot, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Like Bitcoin people talk about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: the risk of consensus failures that this creates.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: VC types are like, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: isn't it expensive and wasteful

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to fund three software teams

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: where you could just be making,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: one quote focused effort.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: They love the word focused.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And Ethereum is not that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but it's amazing despite not being that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Basically, yeah, so that was interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And then there have definitely been other learnings as well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: just from like seeing the chain live

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and seeing what actually is the staking experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like what are the actual incentives

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for all the different participants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So I definitely feel like we're gaining a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: from this sort of one year of trial running the chain

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: before we actually make all of Ethereum depend on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Let me ask perhaps a strange question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but proponents of Bitcoin will say things

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: like Bitcoin fixes everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So why do we need Ethereum

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: versus like Bitcoin plus Lightning Network

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: for scalability and then using Bitcoin

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: with this proof of work for security?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So in this kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: it is perhaps sort of a strange question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but it's a high level question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Why do we need another technology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Yes, it has a bunch of nice features,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but like doesn't Bitcoin fix everything already?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So the thing that always attracted me about Bitcoin

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: is these values of decentralization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: creating these open, provisional systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that anyone can participate in

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and that aren't just going to flop over and die

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: if whoever created them gets bored

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and that are resistant to whoever runs them

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: breaking the rules and all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And I think that pretty strongly

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that these principles are really valid in importance

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: to much more things than just money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Bitcoin is the blockchain for money

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and Ethereum is built from the start

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: as a general purpose blockchain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There is ether, the asset on Ethereum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: but then you can also make decentralized financial things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: what we call DeFi today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: You can make like ENS,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: the decentralized domain name system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: You can make prediction markets on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: You can make totally non-financial systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that just like keep track of whether or not

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: some certificate was signed

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: or whether or not some like cryptographic key got revoked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There's this big long list of like just interesting things

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that you could use about blockchains to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Basically, they are sort of the missing piece

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that we are without them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: the kinds of things that a decentralized computer network

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: can do is very limited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And once you have them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: and a lot of those limitations end up going away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: And so Ethereum was like always from the beginning

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: about that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: It's about like, hey, this isn't just money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: There's so much more that you could do

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: centralized actors.

body.input: And-

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: Hence the smart contracts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: that are running on Ethereum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: general purpose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vitalik Buterin: Ethereum 2.0 | Lex Fridman Podcast #188

body.input: So I think like, I do think that,

body.input: there's a lot more wrong with the world than just money.
