metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: when I was a child and from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And I thought, well, how can it be to build a real one?

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And so then started what turned out to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: like a 15 year obsession with trying to build

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: better snake robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And the first one that I built just sort of slithered

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: sideways, but didn't actually go forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Then I added wheels and building things in real life

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: makes you honest about the friction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: The thing that appeals to me is I love creating

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: the illusion of life, which is what drove me to animation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And if you have a robot with enough degrees

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: of coordinated freedom that move in a kind of biological way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: then it starts to cross the Ancani Valley

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and to see me like a creature rather than a thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And I certainly got that with the early snakes by S3.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I had it able to side wind as well as go directly forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: My wife to be suggested that it would be the ring bearer

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: at our wedding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So it actually went down the aisle carrying the rings

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and got in the local paper for that, which was really fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And this was all done as a hobby.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then at the time the onboard compute

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: was incredibly limited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It was sort of-

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Yeah, so you should explain that these snakes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: the whole idea is that you're trying to run it

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: autonomously so the compute is onboard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Autonomously, onboard power, onboard, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And so the very first one I actually built the controller

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: from discrete logic, because I used to do LSI circuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and things when I was a teenager.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then the second and third one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: the eight bit microprocessors were available

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: with like a whole 256 bytes of RAM,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which you could just about squeeze in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So they were radio controlled rather than autonomous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And really were more about the physicality

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and coordinated motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I've occasionally taken a sidestep into,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: if only I could make it cheaply enough,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: to make a great toy, which has been a lesson

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: in how clockwork is its own magical realm

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that you venture into and learn things about backlash

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and other things you don't take into account

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: as a computer scientist, which is why what seemed

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: like a good idea doesn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So it was quite humbling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then more recently I've been building S9,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which is a much better engineered version of S3

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: where the motors wore out and it doesn't work anymore

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and you can't buy replacements, which is sad given

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that it was such a meaningful one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: S5 was about twice as long

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and looked much more biologically inspired.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I, unlike the typical roboticist, I taper my snakes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: There are good mechanical reasons to do that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but it also makes them look more biological,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: although it means every segment's unique

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: rather than a repetition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which is why most engineers don't do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It actually saves weight and leverage and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And that one is currently on display

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: at the International Spy Museum in Washington, DC.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Not that it's done any spying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It was on YouTube and it got its own conspiracy theory

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: where people thought that it wasn't real

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: because I work at Adobe, it must be fake graphics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And people would write to me, tell me it's real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: You know, say the background doesn't move.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And it's like, it's on a tripod, you know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So that one, but you can see the real thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So it really is true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then the latest one is the first one

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: where I could put a Raspberry Pi,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which leads to all sorts of terrible jokes

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: about pythons and things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: But, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: But this one can have onboard compute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then where my hobby work and my work work

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: are converging is you can now add vision accelerator chips,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which can evaluate neural nets

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and do object recognition and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So both for the snakes and more recently for the spider

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that I've been working on, having desktop level compute

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: is now opening up a whole world of true autonomy

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: with onboard compute, onboard batteries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and still having that sort of biomimetic quality

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that people, that appeals to children in particular,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: they are really drawn to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And adults think they look creepy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but children actually think they look charming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And I gave a series of lectures at Girls Who Code

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: to encourage people to take an interest in technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And at the moment, I'd say they're still more expensive

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: than the value that they add,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which is why they're a great hobby for me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but they're not really a great product.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It makes me think about doing that very early thing I did

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: at Alias with changing the muscle rest lengths.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: If I could do that with a real artificial muscle material,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: then the next snake ideally would use that

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: rather than motors and gearboxes and everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It would be lighter, much stronger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and more continuous and smooth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So it's, I like to say being in research

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: is a license to be curious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And I have the same feeling with my hobby.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It forced me to read biology and be curious about things

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that otherwise would have just been,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: you know, a natural geographic special.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Suddenly I'm thinking, how does that snake move?

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Can I copy it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I look at the trails that sidewinding snakes leave in sand

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and see if my snake robots would do the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So out of something inanimate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I like where you put it, try to bring life into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And beauty. Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then ultimately give it a personality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: which is where the intelligent agent research

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: will converge with the vision and voice synthesis

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: to give it a sense of having,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: not necessarily human level intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I think the Turing test is such a high bar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It's a little bit self-defeating,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but having one that you can have

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: a meaningful conversation with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: especially if you have a reasonably good sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: of what you can say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So not trying to have it so a stranger could walk up

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and have one, but so as a pet owner or a robot pet owner,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: you could know what it thinks about

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and what it can reason about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Or sometimes just a meaningful interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: If you have the kind of interaction you have with a dog,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: sometimes you might have a conversation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but it's usually one way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And nevertheless, it feels like a meaningful connection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And one of the things that I'm trying to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: in the sample audio that will play you

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: is beginning to get towards the point

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: where the reasoning system can explain

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: why it knows something or why it thinks something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And that again creates the sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that it really does know what it's talking about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but also for debugging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: As you get more and more elaborate behavior,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: it's like, why did you decide to do that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: How do you know that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I think the robot's really my muse

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: for helping me think about the future of AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and what to invent next.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So even at Adobe, that's mostly operating in digital world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Do you ever, do you see a future

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: where Adobe even expands into the more physical world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: perhaps, so bringing life not into animations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: but bringing life into physical objects with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: whether it's, well, do you-

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I have to say at the moment, it's a twinkle in my eye.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I think the more likely thing is that we will bring

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: virtual objects into the physical world

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: through augmented reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And many of the ideas that might take five years

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: to build a robot to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: you can do in a few weeks with digital assets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So I think when really intelligent robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: finally become commonplace,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: they won't be that surprising

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: because we'll have been living with those personalities

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: in the virtual sphere for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And then they'll just say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: oh, it's Siri with legs or Alexa on hoofs or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So I can see that well coming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And for now it's still an adventure

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: and we don't know quite what the experience will be like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And it's really exciting to sort of see

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: all of these different strands of my career converge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Yeah, in interesting ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And it is definitely a fun adventure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: So let me end with my favorite poem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: the last few lines of my favorite poem of yours

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: that ponders mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And in some sense, immortality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: as our ideas live through the ideas of others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: through the work of others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: it ends with, do not weep or mourn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: It was enough the little Adames permitted

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: just a single dance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: scatter them as deep as your eyes can see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: I'm content they'll have another chance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: sweeping more centered parts along

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: to join a jostling lifting throng as others danced in me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Beautiful poem, beautiful way to end it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Gavin, thank you so much for talking today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: And thank you for inspiring and empowering

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: millions of people like myself for creating amazing stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Gavin Miller: Adobe Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #23

body.input: Oh, thank you.

body.input: Thank you for the conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Now, here's my conversation with Alex Garland.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: You described the world inside the shimmer in the movie Annihilation as dreamlike, in

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: that it's internally consistent but detached from reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: That leads me to ask, do you think, a philosophical question, I apologize, do you think we might

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: be living in a dream or in a simulation, like the kind that the shimmer creates?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: We human beings here today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I want to sort of separate that out into two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yes, I think we're living in a dream of sorts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: No, I don't think we're living in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think we're living on a planet with a very thin layer of atmosphere and the planet is

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: in a very large space and the space is full of other planets and stars and quasars and

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I don't think those physical objects, I don't think the matter in that universe is simulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think it's there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: We are definitely, it's a whole problem with saying definitely, but in my opinion, I'll

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: just go back to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think it seems very like we're living in a dream state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'm pretty sure we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And I think that's just to do with the nature of how we experience the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: We experience it in a subjective way and the thing I've learned most as I've got older

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: in some respects is the degree to which reality is counterintuitive and that the things that

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: are presented to us as objective turn out not to be objective and quantum mechanics

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: is full of that kind of thing, but actually just day to day life is full of that kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: of thing as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So my understanding of the way the brain works is you get some information, hit your optic

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: nerve and then your brain makes its best guess about what it's seeing or what it's saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: it's seeing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It may or may not be an accurate best guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It might be an inaccurate best guess and that gap, the best guess gap means that we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: essentially living in a subjective state, which means that we're in a dream state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So I think you could enlarge on the dream state in all sorts of ways, but so yes, dream

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: state, no simulation would be where I'd come down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Going further deeper into that direction, you've also described that world as a psychedelia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So on that topic, I'm curious about that world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: On the topic of psychedelic drugs, do you see those kinds of chemicals that modify our

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: perception as a distortion of our perception of reality or a window into another reality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: No, I think what I'd be saying is that we live in a distorted reality and then those

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: kinds of drugs give us a different kind of distorted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Different perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: They just give an alternate distortion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And I think that what they really do is they give a distorted perception which is a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: bit more allied to daydreams or unconscious interests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So if for some reason you're feeling unconsciously anxious at that moment and you take a psychedelic

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: drug, you'll have a more pronounced unpleasant experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And if you're feeling very calm or happy, you might have a good time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But yeah, so if I'm saying we're starting from a premise, our starting point is we were

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: already in the slightly psychedelic state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: What those drugs do is help you go further down an avenue or maybe a slightly different

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: avenue but that's all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So in that movie, Annihilation, the shimmer, this alternate dreamlike state is created

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: by I believe perhaps an alien entity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Of course, everything is up to interpretation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But do you think there's in our world, in our universe, do you think there's intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: life out there and if so, how different is it from us humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Well, one of the things I was trying to do in Annihilation was to offer up a form of

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: alien life that was actually alien.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Because it would often seem to me that in the way we would represent aliens in books

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: or cinema or television or any one of the storytelling mediums is we would always give

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: them very human-like qualities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So they wanted to teach us about galactic federations or they wanted to eat us or they

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: wanted our resources like our water or they want to enslave us or whatever it happens

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But all of these are incredibly human-like motivations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And I was interested in the idea of an alien that was not in any way like us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It didn't share.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Maybe it had a completely different clock speed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Maybe its way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So we're talking about we're looking at each other, we're getting information, light hits

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: our optic nerve, our brain makes the best guess of what we're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Sometimes it's right, something, you know, the thing we were talking about before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: What if this alien doesn't have an optic nerve?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Maybe its way of encountering the space it's in is wholly different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Maybe it has a different relationship with gravity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: The basic laws of physics it operates under might be fundamentally different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It could be a different time scale and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah, or it could be the same laws, it could be the same underlying laws of physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: You know, it's a machine created or it's a creature created in a quantum mechanical

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It just ends up in a very, very different place to the one we end up in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So part of the preoccupation with annihilation was to come up with an alien that was really

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: alien and didn't give us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And it didn't give us and we didn't give it any kind of easy connection between human

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: and the alien.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Because I think it was to do with the idea that you could have an alien that landed on

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: this planet that wouldn't even know we were here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And we might only glancingly know it was here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: That just be this strange point where the Venn diagram is connected, where we could

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: sense each other or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So in the movie, first of all, incredibly original view of what an alien life would

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And it's in that sense, it's a huge success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Let's go inside your imagination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Did the alien that alien entity know anything about humans when it landed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: The idea is you're basically an alien life is trying to reach out to anything that might

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: be able to hear its mechanism of communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Or was it simply, was it just basically their biologists exploring different kinds of stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: that you can find?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But you see, but this is the interesting thing is as soon as you say they're biologists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: you've done the thing of attributing human type motivations to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I don't think, for example, I've got...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: My anxieties relate to things like social media.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So I've got plenty of anxieties about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Which is also driven by artificial intelligence in the sense that there's too much information

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to be able to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: An algorithm has to filter that information and present to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So ultimately the algorithm, a simple, oftentimes simple algorithm, is controlling the flow of

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: information on social media.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So that's another form of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But at least my sense of it, I might be wrong, but my sense of it is that the algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: have an either conscious or unconscious bias, which is created by the people who are making

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: the algorithms and sort of delineating the areas to which those algorithms are going

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to lean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And so for example, the kind of thing I'd be worried about is that it hasn't been thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: about enough how dangerous it is to allow algorithms to create echo chambers, say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But that doesn't seem to me to be about the AI or the algorithm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It's the naivety of the people who are constructing the algorithms to do that thing, if you see

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: what I mean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So in your new series, Devs, and we could speak more broadly, there's a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Let's talk about the people constructing those algorithms, which in our modern society, Silicon

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Valley, those algorithms happen to be a source of a lot of income because of advertisements.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So let me ask sort of a question about those people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Are there current concerns and failures on social media, their naivety?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I can't pronounce that word well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Are they naive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Are they...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I use that word carefully, but evil in intent or misaligned in intent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think that's a... do they mean well and just have an unintended consequence or is

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: there something dark in them that results in them creating a company, results in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: super competitive drive to be successful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And those are the people that will end up controlling the algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: At a guess, I'd say there are instances of all those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So sometimes I think it's naivety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Sometimes I think it's extremely dark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And sometimes I think people are not being naive or dark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And then in those instances, they're sometimes generating things that are very benign and

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: other times generating things that despite their best intentions are not very benign.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It's something...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think the reason why I don't get anxious about AI in terms of, or at least AIs that

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: have, I don't know, a relationship with some sort of relationship with humans is that I

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: think that's the stuff we're quite well equipped to understand how to mitigate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: The problem is issues that relate actually to the power of humans or the wealth of humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And that's where it's dangerous here and now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So what I see...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'll tell you what I sometimes feel about Silicon Valley is that it's like Wall Street

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: in the 80s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It's rabidly capitalistic, absolutely rabidly capitalistic and it's rabidly greedy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But whereas in the 80s, the sense one had of Wall Street was that these people knew

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: they were sharks and in a way relished in being sharks and dressed in sharp suits and

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: lauded over other people and felt good about doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Silicon Valley has managed to hide its voracious Wall Street-like capitalism behind hipster

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: t-shirts and cool cafes in the place where they set up there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And so that obfuscates what's really going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: What's really going on is the absolute voracious pursuit of money and power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So that's where it gets shaky for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So that veneer, and you explore that brilliantly, that veneer of virtue that Silicon Valley

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: has...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Which they believe themselves, I'm sure, for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I hope to be one of those people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And I believe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So as maybe a devil's advocate term poorly used in this case, what if some of them really

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: are trying to build a better world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'm sure I think some of them are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think I've spoken to ones who I believe in their heart feel they're building a better

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Are they not able to in a sense?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: No, they may or may not be, but it's just a zone with a lot of bullshit flying about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And there's also another thing, which is this actually goes back to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I always thought about some sports that later turned out to be corrupt in the way that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: sport...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Like who won the boxing match or how a football match got thrown or cricket match or whatever

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: it happened to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And I used to think, well, look, if there's a lot of money and there really is a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: money, people stand to make millions or even billions, you will find corruption that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So it's in the nature of its voracious appetite that some people will be corrupt and some

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: people will exploit and some people will exploit whilst thinking they're doing something good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But there are also people who I think are very, very smart and very benign and actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: very self-aware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And so I'm not trying to wipe out the motivations of this entire area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: There are people in that world who scare the hell out of me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah, sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'm a little bit naive in that I don't care at all about money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And so...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: You might be one of the good guys.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But so the thought is, but I don't have money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So my thought is if you give me a billion dollars, it would change nothing and I would

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: spend it right away on resting it right back and creating a good world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But your intuition is that billion, there's something about that money that maybe slowly

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: corrupts the people around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: There's somebody gets in that corrupts your soul the way you view the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Money does corrupt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: We know that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But there's a different sort of problem aside from just the money corrupts thing that we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: familiar with throughout history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And it's more about the sense of reinforcement an individual gets, which is so...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It effectively works like the reason I earned all this money and so much more money than

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: anyone else is because I'm very gifted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'm actually a bit smarter than they are, or I'm a lot smarter than they are, and I

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: can see the future in the way they can't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And maybe some of those people are not particularly smart, they're very lucky, or they're very

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: talented entrepreneurs, and there's a difference between...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So in other words, the acquisition of the money and power can suddenly start to feel

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: like evidence of virtue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And it's not evidence of virtue, it might be evidence of completely different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: As brilliantly put, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So I think one of the fundamental drivers of my current morality...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Let me just represent nerds in general, of all kinds, is constant self-doubt and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: signals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'm very sensitive to signals from people that tell me I'm doing the wrong thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But when there's a huge inflow of money, you just put it brilliantly that that could become

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: an overpowering signal that everything you do is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And so your moral compass can just get thrown off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: That is not contained to Silicon Valley, that's across the board.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: In general, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Like I said, I'm from the Soviet Union, the current president is convinced, I believe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: actually he wants to do really good by the country and by the world, but his moral compass

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: may be off because...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah, I mean, it's the interesting thing about evil, which is that I think most people who

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: do spectacularly evil things think themselves they're doing really good things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: They're not there thinking, I am a sort of incarnation of Satan, they're thinking, I've

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: seen a way to fix the world and everyone else is wrong, here I go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: In fact, I'm having a fascinating conversation with a historian of Stalin and he took power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: he actually got more power than almost any person in history and he wanted, he didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: want power, he just wanted, he truly, and this is what people don't realize, he truly

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: believed that communism will make for a better world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And he wanted power, he wanted to destroy the competition to make sure that we actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: make communism work in the Soviet Union and spread it across the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: He was trying to do good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think it's typically the case that that's what people think they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And I think that, but you don't need to go to Stalin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I mean, Stalin, I think Stalin probably got pretty crazy, but actually that's another

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: part of it, which is that the other thing that comes from being convinced of your own

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: virtue is that then you stop listening to the modifiers around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And that tends to drive people crazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It's other people that keep us sane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77
