metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: If something appears conscious, is it conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: You mentioned the smile, which seems to be something done...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: That's a really good indication because it's a tree falling in the forest with nobody there

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to hear it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But does the appearance from a robotics perspective of consciousness mean consciousness to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I don't think you could say that fully because I think you could then easily have a thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: experiment which said, we will create something which we know is not conscious, but is going

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to give a very, very good account of seeming conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And also it would be a particularly bad test where humans are involved because humans are

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: so quick to project sentience into things that don't have sentience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So someone could have their computer playing up and feel as if their computer is being

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: malevolent to them when it clearly isn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And so of all the things to judge consciousness, us...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Humans are bad at...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: We're empathy machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So the flip side of that, the argument there is because we just attribute consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to everything almost and anthropomorphize everything, including Roombas, that maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: consciousness is not real, that we just attribute consciousness to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So you have a sense that there is something really special going on in our mind that makes

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: us unique and gives us subjective experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: There's something very interesting going on in our minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I'm slightly worried about the word special because it nudges towards metaphysics and

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: maybe even magic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: In some ways, something magic-like, which I don't think is there at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I mean, if you think about...

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: There's an idea called panpsychism that says consciousness isn't everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah, I don't buy that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I don't buy that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So the idea that there is a thing that it would be like to be the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I don't buy that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I think that consciousness is a thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: My sort of broad modification is that usually the more I find out about things, the more

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: illusory our instinct is and is leading us into a different direction about what that

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: thing actually is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: That happens, it seems to me, in modern science, that happens a hell of a lot, whether it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: to do with even how big or small things are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So my sense is that consciousness is a thing, but it isn't quite the thing or maybe very

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: different from the thing that we instinctively think it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So it's there, it's very interesting, but we may be in sort of quite fundamentally misunderstanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: it for reasons that are based on intuition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So I have to ask, this is kind of an interesting question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: The Ex Machina, for many people, including myself, is one of the greatest AI films ever

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It's number two for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Thanks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah, it's definitely not number one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: If it was number one, I'd really have to anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Whenever you grow up with something, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Whenever you grow up with something, it's in the mud.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But there's one of the things that people bring up and can't please everyone, including

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: The reason I first reacted to the film is the idea of the lone genius.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: This is the criticism that people say, sort of me as an AI researcher, I'm trying to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: what Nathan is trying to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So there's a brilliant series called Chernobyl.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yes, it's fantastic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Absolutely spectacular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I mean, they've got so many things brilliant and right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But one of the things, again, the criticism there-

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Into one character that represents all nuclear scientists, Ilana Komyech.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: It's a composite character that represents all the scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: How do you think about the lone genius?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Well, I'd say this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: The series I'm doing at the moment is a critique in part of the lone genius concept.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: So yes, I'm sort of oppositional and either agnostic or atheistic about that as a concept.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I mean, not entirely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Whether lone is the right word, broadly isolated, but Newton clearly exists in a sort of bubble

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: of himself in some respects, so does Shakespeare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Do you think we would have an iPhone without Steve Jobs?

body.input: How much contribution from a genius-

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But Steve Jobs clearly isn't a lone genius because there's too many other people in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: sort of superstructure around him who are absolutely fundamental to that journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But you're saying Newton, but that's a scientific, so there's an engineering element to building

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: Ava.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: But just to say, X Machina is really, it's a thought experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: I mean, so it's a construction of putting four people in a house.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: machine parts.

body.input: Did the people building the machine parts know what they were creating and how did they

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: get there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

body.input: And it's a thought experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Alex Garland: Ex Machina, Devs, Annihilation, and the Poetry of Science | Lex Fridman Podcast #77

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I think our artificial intelligence will be smarter in the future. For a Mars mission, it's a great question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: The reality is for a Mars mission, we need fully autonomous systems. We will get humans, but they have to be fully autonomous.

body.input: And that's the most important concept because there's not going to be a mission control on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: 20 minute time lag, there's just no way you're going to control it. So people have to be fully autonomous as well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: but all of our systems as well. And so that's the big design challenge. So that's why we test them out on the Moon as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: When we have a, okay, a few seconds, three second time lag, you can test them out. We have to really get autonomous exploration down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: they have resources, that's in situ resource utilization and everything else they brought with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: So we have to, I think, have that mindset for exploration. Again, back to the Moon, it's more the testing ground,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: the proving ground with technologies. But when we get to Mars, it's so far away that we need fully autonomous systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: So I think that's where, again, AI and autonomy come in, really robust autonomy, things that we don't have today yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: So they're on the drawing boards, but we really need to test them out because that's what we're up against.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: So fully autonomous, meaning like self-sufficient, there's still a role for the human in that picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Do you think there'll be a time when AI systems just beyond doing fully autonomous flight control will also help or even take mission decisions like Hal did?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: That's interesting. It depends. I mean, they're going to be designed by humans. I think as you mentioned, humans are always in the loop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I mean, we might be on Earth, we might be in orbit on Mars, maybe the systems that landers down on the surface of Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: But I think we are right now just on Earth-based systems, AI systems that are incredibly capable and training them with all the data that we have now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: petabytes of data from Earth. What I care about for the autonomy and AI right now, how we're applying it in research, is to look at Earth and look at climate systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I mean, it's not for Mars to me today. Right now, AI is to eyes on Earth, all of our space data, compiling that using supercomputers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: because we have so much information and knowledge and we need to get that into people's hands.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: First, there's the educational issue with climate and our changing climate. Then we need to change human behavior. That's the biggie.

body.input: This next decade, it's urgent that we take care of our own spaceship, which is Spaceship Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I simply put, Earth doesn't need us, but we really need Earth. All of humanity needs to live in balance with Earth because Earth has been here a long time before we ever showed up, and it'll be here a long time after.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: It's just a matter of how do we want to live with all living beings, much more in balance because we need to take care of the Earth, and right now we're not. That's the urgency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I think it is the next decade to try to live much more sustainably, live more in balance with Earth. I think the human species has a great long optimistic future, but we have to act. It's urgent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Spaceship Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: We're all astronauts on Spaceship Earth, and this is our mission. This is our mission to take care of the planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: And yet, as we explore out from our Spaceship Earth here out into space, what do you think the next 50, 100, 200 years look like for space exploration?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I'm optimistic, so I think that we'll have lots of people, thousands of people, tens of thousands of people, who knows, maybe millions in low Earth orbit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: That's just a place that we're going to have people and actually some industry, manufacturing, things like that. That dream, I hope we realize, getting people to the Moon so I can envision a lot of people on the Moon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Again, it's a great place to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Living or visiting?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Probably visiting and living if you want to. Most people are going to want to come back to Earth, I think, but there'll be some people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: And it's not such a long...

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Good view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: It's a good view. It's a beautiful view. So I think that we will have many people on the Moon as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I think there'll be some people, you told me, wow, hundreds of years out. So we'll have people, we'll be interplanetary for sure as a species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: So I think we'll be on the Moon. I think we'll be on Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Venus, no, it's already a runaway greenhouse gas, so not a great place for science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Jupiter, all within the solar system, great place for all of our scientific probes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: I don't see so much in terms of human physical presence. We'll be exploring them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: So we live in our minds there because we're exploring them and going on those journeys, but it's really our choice in terms of our decisions of how in balance we're going to be living here on the Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: When do you think the first woman, first person will step on Mars?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Step on Mars? Well, I'm going to do everything I can to make sure it happens in the 2030s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51
Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Say mid-2025, 2035, we'll be on the Moon and hopefully with more people than us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: But first with a few astronauts, it'll be global, international folks, but we really need those 10 years, I think, on the Moon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: And then so by later in the decade, in the 2030s, we'll have all the technology and know-how and we need to get that human mission to Mars done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: We'll live in exciting times. And, Deva, thank you so much for leading the way and thank you for talking today. I really appreciate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dava Newman: Space Exploration, Space Suits, and Life on Mars | Lex Fridman Podcast #51

body.input: Thank you. My pleasure.

body.input: The following is a conversation with Peter Abil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: He's a professor at UC Berkeley and the director of the Berkeley Robotics Learning Lab.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: He's one of the top researchers in the world working on how we make robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: understand and interact with the world around them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: especially using imitation and deep reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: This conversation is part of the MIT course on Artificial General Intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and the Artificial Intelligence podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: If you enjoy it, please subscribe on YouTube, iTunes, or your podcast provider of choice,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: or simply connect with me on Twitter at Lex Friedman, spelled F-R-I-D.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And now, here's my conversation with Peter Abil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You've mentioned that if there was one person you could meet, it would be Roger Federer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So let me ask, when do you think we'll have a robot that fully autonomously can beat Roger Federer at tennis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Roger Federer level player at tennis?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Well, first, if you can make it happen for me to meet Roger, let me know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: In terms of getting a robot to beat him at tennis, it's kind of an interesting question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: because for a lot of the challenges we think about in AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: the software is really the missing piece.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But for something like this, the hardware is nowhere near either.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: To really have a robot that can physically run around,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: the Boston Dynamics robots are starting to get there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but still not really human level ability to run around and then swing a racket.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So you think that's a hardware problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I don't think it's a hardware problem only.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I think it's a hardware and a software problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I think it's both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I think they'll have independent progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So I'd say the hardware maybe in 10, 15 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: On clay, not grass.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, grass is probably harder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Well, the clay, I'm not sure what's harder, grass or clay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: The clay involves sliding, which might be harder to master actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But you're not limited to bipedal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, I'm sure there's no room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Well, if we can build a machine, it's a whole different question, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: If you can say, OK, this robot can be on wheels, it can move around on wheels

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and can be designed differently, then I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that can be done sooner probably than a full humanoid type of setup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: What do you think is swing a racket?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So you've worked at basic manipulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: How hard do you think is the task of swinging a racket?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Would it be able to hit a nice backhand or a forehand?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Let's say we just set up stationary, a nice robot arm, let's say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: a standard industrial arm, and it can watch the ball come and swing the racket.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's a good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I'm not sure it would be super hard to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, I'm sure it would require a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: If we do it with reinforcement learning, it would require a lot of trial and error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's not going to swing it right the first time around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But yeah, I don't see why I couldn't swing it the right way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I think it's learnable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I think if you set up a ball machine, let's say, on one side

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and then a robot with a tennis racket on the other side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I think it's learnable and maybe a little bit of pre-training and simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Yeah, I think that's feasible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I think the swing the racket is feasible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It would be very interesting to see how much precision it can get.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because I mean, that's where some of the human players

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: can hit it on the lines, which is very high precision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: With spin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: The spin is an interesting, where the RL can learn to put a spin on the ball.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Well, you got me interested.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Maybe someday we'll set this up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You got me intrigued.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Your answer is basically, OK, for this problem, it sounds fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But for the general problem of a tennis player,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: we might be a little bit farther away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: What's the most impressive thing you've seen a robot do in the physical world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So physically, for me, it's the Boston Dynamics videos always just ring home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I'm just super impressed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Recently, the robot running up the stairs, doing the parkour type thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, yes, we don't know what's underneath.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They don't really write a lot of detail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But even if it's hard coded underneath, which it might or might not

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: be, just the physical abilities of doing that parkour,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that's a very impressive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So have you met Spotmini or any of those robots in person?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Met Spotmini last year in April at the Mars event that GFBs was organizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They brought it out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And it was nicely following around Jeff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: When Jeff left the room, they had it follow him along,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: which is pretty impressive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So I think there's some confidence to know that there's no learning going

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: on in those robots, the psychology of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So while knowing that, while knowing there's not,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: if there's any learning going on, it's very limited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I met Spotmini earlier this year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And knowing everything that's going on, having one-on-one interaction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: so I get to spend some time alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And there's immediately a deep connection on the psychological level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Even though you know the fundamentals, how it works,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: there's something magical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So do you think about the psychology of interacting

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: with robots in the physical world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You just showed me the PR2, the robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And there was a little bit something like a face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It had a little bit something like a face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: There's something that immediately draws you to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Do you think about that aspect of the robotics problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Well, it's very hard with Brad here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: We'll give him a name, Berkeley Robot for the Elimination of Tedious Tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's very hard to not think of the robot as a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And it seems like everybody calls him a he for whatever reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But that also makes it more a person than if it was a it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And it seems pretty natural to think of it that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: This past weekend really struck me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I've seen Pepper many times on videos.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But then I was at an event organized by, this was by Fidelity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And they had scripted Pepper to help moderate some sessions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And they had scripted Pepper to have the personality of a child a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And it was very hard to not think of it as its own person in some sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because it was just kind of jumping, it would just jump in the conversation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: making it very interactive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Moderator would be saying, Pepper would just jump in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Hold on, how about me?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Can I participate in this doing it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Just like, OK, this is like a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And that was 100% scripted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And even then, it was hard not to have that sense of somehow there

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is something there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So as we have robots interact in this physical world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is that a signal that could be used in reinforcement learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You've worked a little bit in this direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But do you think that that psychology can be somehow pulled in?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Yes, that's a question I would say a lot of people ask.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I think part of why they ask it is they're thinking about how unique

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: are we really still as people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: After they see some results, they see a computer play Go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They say, computer, do this, that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They're like, OK, but can it really have emotion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Can it really interact with us in that way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And then once you're around robots, you already start feeling it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I think that maybe methodologically, the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that I think of it is if you run something like reinforcement

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: learning, it's about optimizing some objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And there's no reason that the objective couldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: be tied into how much does a person like interacting with this system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And why could not the reinforcement learning system

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: optimize for the robot being fun to be around?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: on a person having a mind in their own mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that the robot would figure out over time, oh, this kind of thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So when I first picked up Richard Sutton's reinforcement learning book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: before this deep learning, before the reemergence of neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: as a powerful mechanism for machine learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: RL seemed to me like magic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It was beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So that seemed like what intelligence is, RL, reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So how do you think we can possibly learn anything about the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: when the reward for the actions is delayed, is so sparse?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Where is, why do you think RL works?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Why do you think you can learn anything under such sparse rewards,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: whether it's regular reinforcement learning or deep reinforcement learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's your intuition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: The counterpart of that is, why is RL, why

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: does it need so many samples, so many experiences to learn from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because really what's happening is when you have a sparse reward,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: you do something maybe for like, I don't know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: you take 100 actions and then you get a reward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Or maybe you get like a score of three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I'm like, OK, three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Not sure what that means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You go again and now I get two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And now you know that that sequence of 100 actions

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that you did the second time around somehow was worse

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: than the sequence of 100 actions you did the first time around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But that's tough to now know which one of those were better or worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Some might have been good and bad and either one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so that's why I need so many experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But once you have enough experiences, effectively RL is teasing that apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's starting to say, OK, what is consistently there

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: when you get a higher reward and what's consistently there

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: when you get a lower reward?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And then kind of the magic of sometimes the policy grant update

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is to say, now let's update the neural network

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to make the actions that were kind of present when things are good

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: more likely and make the actions that are present

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: when things are not as good less likely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So that's that is the counterpoint.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But it seems like you would need to run it a lot more than you do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: even though right now people could say that RL is very inefficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But it seems to be way more efficient than one would imagine on paper

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that the simple updates to the policy, the policy gradient,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that somehow you can learn exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You just said, what are the common actions

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that seem to produce some good results?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: That that somehow can learn anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It seems counterintuitive, at least.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Is there some intuition behind it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So I think there's a few ways to think about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: The way I tend to think about it mostly originally when

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: so when we started working on deep reinforcement learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: here at Berkeley, which is maybe 2011, 12, 13, around that time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: John Schulman was a PhD student, initially kind of driving it forward here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And the way we thought about it at the time was,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: if you think about rectified linear units or kind of rectifier type neural networks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: what do you get?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You get something that's piecewise linear feedback control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And if you look at the literature, linear feedback control

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is extremely successful, can solve many, many problems surprisingly well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I remember, for example, when we did helicopter flight,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: if you're in a stationary flight regime, not a non-stationary,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but a stationary flight regime like hover,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: you can use linear feedback control to stabilize a helicopter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: very complex dynamical system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But the controller is relatively simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so I think that's a big part of it is that if you do feedback control,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: even though the system you control can be very, very complex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: often relatively simple control architectures can already do a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But then also just linear is not good enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so one way you can think of these neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is that sometimes they tile the space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: which people were already trying to do more by hand

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: or with finite state machines, say, this linear controller here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: this linear controller here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Neural network learns to tile the space and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: linear controller here, another linear controller here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but it's more subtle than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so it's benefiting from this linear control aspect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: it's benefiting from the tiling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but it's somehow tiling it one dimension at a time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because if, let's say, you have a two-layer network,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: even that hidden layer, you make a transition from active to inactive

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: or the other way around, that is essentially one axis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but not axis aligned, but one direction that you change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so you have this kind of very gradual tiling of the space

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: where you have a lot of sharing between the linear controllers

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that tile the space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And that was always my intuition as to why to expect

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that this might work pretty well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's essentially leveraging the fact that linear feedback control

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is so good, but of course not enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And this is a gradual tiling of the space

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: with linear feedback controls that share a lot of expertise across them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So that's really nice intuition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But do you think that scales to the more and more general problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: of when you start going up the number of dimensions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: when you start going down in terms of how often you get a clean reward signal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Does that intuition carry forward to those crazier, weirder worlds

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that we think of as the real world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So I think where things get really tricky in the real world

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: compared to the things we've looked at so far with great success

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: in reinforcement learning is the time scales,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: which takes us to an extreme.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So when you think about the real world, I mean, I don't know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: maybe some student decided to do a PhD here, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Okay, that's a decision, that's a very high level decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But if you think about their lives, I mean, any person's life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: it's a sequence of muscle fiber contractions and relaxations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and that's how you interact with the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And that's a very high frequency control thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but it's ultimately what you do and how you affect the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Until I guess we have brain readings, you can maybe do it slightly differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But typically that's how you affect the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And the decision of doing a PhD is like so abstract

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: relative to what you're actually doing in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I think that's where credit assignment becomes just completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: beyond what any current RL algorithm can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And we need hierarchical reasoning at a level that is just not available at all yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Where do you think we can pick up hierarchical reasoning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: By which mechanisms?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Yeah, so maybe let me highlight what I think the limitations are

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: of what already was done 20, 30 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: In fact, you'll find reasoning systems that reason over relatively long horizons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but the problem is that they were not grounded in the real world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So people would have to hand design some kind of logical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: dynamical descriptions of the world, and that didn't tie into perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so it didn't tie into real objects and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so that was a big gap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Now with deep learning, we start having the ability to really see with sensors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: process that and understand what's in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so it's a good time to try to bring these things together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I see a few ways of getting there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: One way to get there would be to say deep learning can get bolted on somehow

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to some of these more traditional approaches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Now bolted on would probably mean you need to do some kind of end to end training

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: where you say my deep learning processing somehow leads to a representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that in term uses some kind of traditional underlying dynamical systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that can be used for planning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And that's, for example, the direction Aviv Tamar and Thonard Kuratach here

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: have been pushing with causal info again, and of course, other people too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: That's one way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10
