body.input: A lot of people have concern about safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: How do you think about AI safety as you build robots that

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: are operating in the physical world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: How do you approach this problem in an engineering kind of way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: in a systematic way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So when a robot is doing things, you kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: have a few notions of safety to worry about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: One is that the robot is physically strong

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and, of course, could do a lot of damage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Same for cars, which we can think of as robots do in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And this could be completely unintentional.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So it could be not the kind of long-term AI safety concerns

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that, OK, AI is smarter than us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And now what do we do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But it could be just very practical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: OK, this robot, if it makes a mistake,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: what are the results going to be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Of course, simulation comes in a lot there to test in simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's a difficult question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I'm always wondering, like, I always wonder,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: let's say you look at, let's go back to driving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: because a lot of people know driving well, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: What do we do to test somebody for driving, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Get a driver's license.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: What do they really do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, you fill out some tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And then you drive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I mean, in suburban California,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that driving test is just you drive around the block, pull over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You do a stop sign successfully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And then you pull over again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And you're pretty much done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And you're like, OK, if a self-driving car did that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: would you trust it that it can drive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I'd be like, no, that's not enough for me to trust it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But somehow, for humans, we've figured out

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that somebody being able to do that is representative of them

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: being able to do a lot of other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so I think somehow, for humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: we figured out representative tests of what

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: it means if you can do this, what you can really do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Of course, testing humans, humans don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: want to be tested at all times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Self-driving cars or robots could be tested more often,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: probably.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You can have replicas that get tested

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and are known to be identical because they use the same neural

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: net and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But still, I feel like we don't have this kind of unit tests

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: or proper tests for robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And I think there's something very interesting to be thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: about there, especially as you update things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Your software improves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You have a better self-driving car suite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You update it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: How do you know it's indeed more capable on everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: than what you had before, that you didn't have any bad things

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: creep into it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So I think that's a very interesting direction

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: of research, that there is no real solution yet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: except that somehow for humans, we do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because we say, OK, you have a driving test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You passed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You can go on the road now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And humans have accidents every million or 10 million miles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: something pretty phenomenal compared

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to that short test that is being done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So let me ask, you've mentioned that Andrew Ng, by example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: showed you the value of kindness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Do you think the space of policies, good policies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: for humans and for AI is populated by policies

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that with kindness or ones that are the opposite, exploitation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: even evil?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So if you just look at the sea of policies

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: we operate under as human beings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: or if AI system had to operate in this real world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: do you think it's really easy to find policies

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that are full of kindness, like we naturally fall into them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Or is it a very hard optimization problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, there is two optimizations

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: happening for humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So for humans, there is the very long-term optimization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: which evolution has done for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And we're kind of predisposed to like certain things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And that's in some sense what makes our learning easier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because we know things like pain and hunger and thirst.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And the fact that we know about those

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is not something that we were taught.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: That's kind of innate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: When we're hungry, we're unhappy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: When we're thirsty, we're unhappy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: When we have pain, we're unhappy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And ultimately, evolution built that into us

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to think about those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so I think there is a notion that it seems somehow

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: for humans evolved in general to prefer to get along

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: in some ways, but at the same time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: also to be very territorial and kind of centric

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to their own tribe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It seems like that's the kind of space we converged onto.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, I'm not an expert in anthropology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: but it seems like we're very kind of good

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: within our own tribe, but need to be taught

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to be nice to other tribes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: If you look at Steven Pinker, he highlights this pretty nicely

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: in Better Angels of Our Nature, where

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: he talks about violence decreasing over time

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: consistently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So whatever tension, whatever teams we pick,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: it seems that the long arc of history

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: goes towards us getting along more and more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I hope so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So do you think it's possible to teach

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: RL-based robots this kind of kindness, this kind of ability

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to interact with humans, this kind of policy, even to a let

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: me ask a fun one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Do you think it's possible to teach RL-based robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to love a human being and to inspire that human

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to love the robot back?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So to like a RL-based algorithm that leads to a happy marriage?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: That's an interesting question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Maybe I'll answer it with another question, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Because I mean, but I'll come back to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So another question I can have is, OK, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: how close does some people's happiness

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: get from interacting with just a really nice dog?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, dogs, you come home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: That's what dogs do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They greet you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They're excited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Makes you happy when you come home to your dog.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: You're just like, OK, this is exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: They're always happy when I'm here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I mean, if they don't greet you because maybe whatever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: your partner took them on a trip or something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: you might not be nearly as happy when you get home, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so it seems like the level of reasoning a dog has

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: is pretty sophisticated, but then it's still not yet

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: at the level of human reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so it seems like we don't even

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: need to achieve human level reasoning

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: to get very strong affection with humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: And so my thinking is, why not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Why couldn't, with an AI, couldn't we

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: achieve the kind of level of affection

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: that humans feel among each other or with friendly animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and so forth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: It's a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Is it a good thing for us or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: That's another thing, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: But I don't see why not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Why not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: So Elon Musk says love is the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Maybe he should say love is the objective function

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: and then RL is the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Oh, maybe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Peter, thank you so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: I don't want to take up more of your time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Pieter Abbeel: Deep Reinforcement Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #10

body.input: Thank you so much for talking today.

body.input: Great to have you visit.
