body.input: the brain is something that has inspired me ever since I learned about her work. And in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I invited her to speak at the AGI series I organized at MIT several years ago. But as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: little twist, instead of a lecture, we did a conversation in front of the class. I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that was one of the early moments that led me to start this very podcast. It was scary, exciting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: scary, and gratifying, which is exactly what life is all about. And it's kind of funny how life turns

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: on little moments like these that at the time don't seem to be anything out of the ordinary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: If you enjoy this thing, subscribe on YouTube, review it with 5 stars on Apple Podcasts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: follow on Spotify, support on Patreon, or connect with me on Twitter at Lex Friedman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Lisa Feldman Barrett. Since we'll talk a lot about the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: today, do you think, let's ask the craziest question, do you think there is other intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: life out there in the universe? Honestly, I've been asking myself lately if there's intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: life on this planet. You know, I have to think probabilities suggest yes. And also, secretly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I think I just hope that's true. It would be really, I know scientists aren't supposed to have

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: hopes and dreams, but I think it would be really cool. And I also think it would be really sad if

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it wasn't the case. If we really were alone, that would be, that would seem profoundly sad, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So it's exciting to you and not scary?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, no. You know, I take a lot of comfort in curiosity. It's a great resource for dealing

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: with stress. So I'm learning all about mushrooms and octopuses and all kinds of stuff. And so for

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: me, this counts, I think, in the realm of awe. But also, I think I'm somebody who cultivates awe

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: deliberately on purpose to feel like a speck. You know, I find it a relief occasionally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: To feel small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: To feel small in a profoundly large and interesting universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So maybe to dig more technically on the question of intelligence, do you think it's difficult for

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: intelligent life to arise like it did on Earth? From everything you've written and studied about

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the brain, how magical of a thing is it in terms of the odds it takes to arise?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, so, you know, magic is just... Don't get me wrong. I mean, I like a magic show as much as the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: next person. My husband was a magician at one time. But, you know, magic is just a bunch of stuff that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: we don't really understand how it works yet. So I would say from what I understand, there are some

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: major steps in the course of evolution that at the beginning of life, the step from single cell to

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: multicellular organisms, things like that, which are really not known. I think for me, the question

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is not so much could it, you know, what's the likelihood that it would happen again as much as

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: what are the steps and how long would it take? And if it were to happen again on Earth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: would we end up with the same menu of life forms that we currently have now? And I think the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: answer is probably no, right? There's just so much about evolution that is stochastic and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: driven by chance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But the question is whether that menu would be equally delicious, meaning like there'd be rich

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: complexity of the kind of like, would we get dolphins and humans or whoever else falls in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: category of weirdly intelligent, seemingly intelligent, however we define that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, I think that has to be true if you just look at the range of creatures who've gone extinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I mean, if you look at the range of creatures that are on the Earth now, it's incredible. And,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you know, it's sort of tried to say that, but it actually is really incredible. Particularly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I don't know, I mean, animals, there are animals that seem really ordinary until you watch them

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: closely and then they become miraculous, you know, like certain types of birds, which do very

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: miraculous things, build, you know, bowers and do dances and all these really funky things. And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: they're really hard to explain with a standard evolutionary story, although, you know, people

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: have them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Birds are weird. They do a lot of for mating purposes. They have a concept of beauty that I

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: haven't quite, maybe you know much better, but it doesn't seem to fit evolutionary arguments well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: It does fit. Well, it depends, right? So I think you're talking about the evolution of beauty, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: book that was written recently by, was it from, was that his name? Richard Frum, I think at Yale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Oh, actually, no, I didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Oh, it's a great book. It's very controversial though, because he's making an argument that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the question about birds and some other animals is why would they engage in such metabolically

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: costly displays when it doesn't improve their fitness at all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And the answer that he gives is the answer that Darwin gave, which is sexual selection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: not natural selection, but you know, selection can occur for all kinds of reasons. There could be

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: artificial selection, which is when we breed animals, right? Which is actually how Darwin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that observation helped Darwin come to the idea of natural selection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Oh, interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And then there's sexual selection, meaning, and the argument that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and then there's sexual selection, meaning, and the argument that I think his name is Frum makes

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is that it's the pleasure, the selection pressure is the pleasure of female birds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which as a woman and as someone who studies affect, that's a great answer. I actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: think there probably is natural, I think there is an aspect of natural selection to it, which he

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: maybe hasn't considered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But you were saying the reason we brought up birds is the life we've got now seems to be quite

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, so you peek into the ocean, peek into the sky, there are miraculous creatures, look at

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: creatures who've gone extinct and you know, in science fiction stories, you couldn't dream up

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: something as interesting. So my guess is that, you know, intelligent life evolves in many different

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: ways, even on this planet, there isn't one form of intelligence, there's not one brain that gives

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you intelligence, there are lots of different brain structures that can give you intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So my guess is that the menagerie might not look exactly the way that it looks now, but it would

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: certainly be as interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But if we look at the human brain versus the brains, or whatever you call them, the mechanisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of intelligence in our ancestors, even early ancestors, that you write about, for example, in

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: your new book, what's the difference between the fanciest brain we got, which is the human brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and the ancestor brains that it came from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, I think it depends on how far back you want to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: You go all the way back, right? In your book. So what's the interesting comparison, would you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, first of all, I wouldn't say that the human brain is the fanciest brain we've got. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: an octopus brain is pretty different and pretty fancy, and they can do some pretty amazing things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that we cannot do. You know, we can't grow back limbs, we can't change color and texture, we can't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: comport ourselves and squeeze ourselves into a little crevice. I mean, these are things that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: invent, these are like superhero abilities that we invent in stories, right? We can't do any of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: those things. And so the human brain is certainly, we can certainly do some things that other animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: can't do that seem pretty impressive to us. But I would say that there are a number of animal brains

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which seem pretty impressive to me that can do interesting things and really impressive things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that we can't do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I mean, with your work on how emotions are made and so on, you kind of repaint the view of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: as less glamorous, I suppose, than you would otherwise think. Or like, I guess you draw a thread

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that connects all brains together in terms of homeostasis and all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, I wouldn't say that the human brain is any less miraculous than anybody else would say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I just think that there are other brain structures which are also miraculous. And I also think that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: there are a number of things about the human brain which we share with other vertebrates,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: other animals with backbones, but that we share these miraculous things. But we can do some things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in abundance. And we can also do some things with our brains together, working together that other

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: animals can't do, or at least we haven't discovered their ability to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, the social thing. That's one of the things you write about. How do you make sense of the fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: like the book Sapiens, and the fact that we're able to kind of connect, like network our brains

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: together, like you write about. I'll try to stop saying that. Is that some kind of feature

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that's built into there? Is that unique to our human brains? How do you make sense of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: What I would say is that our ability to coordinate with each other is not unique

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to humans. There are lots of animals who can do that. But what we do with that coordination

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is unique because of some of the structural features in our brains. And it's not that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: other animals don't have those structural features. It's we have them in abundance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So the human brain is not larger than you would expect it to be for a primate of our size. If you

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: took a chimpanzee and you grew it to the size of a human, that chimpanzee would have a brain that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: was the size of a human brain. So there's nothing special about our brain in terms of its size.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: There's nothing special about our brains in terms of the basic blueprint that builds our brain from

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: an embryo is the basic blueprint that builds all mammalian brains and maybe even all vertebrate

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brains. It's just that because of its size and particularly because of the size of the cerebral

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: cortex, which is a part that people mistakenly attribute to rationality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Why mistakenly? Is that where all the clever stuff happens?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, no, it really isn't. And I will also say that lots of clever stuff happens in animals who

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: don't have a cerebral cortex. But because of the size of the cerebral cortex and because of some of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the features that are enhanced by that size, that gives us the capacity to do things like build

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: civilizations and coordinate with each other, not just to manipulate the physical world, but to add

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to it in very profound ways. Other animals can cooperate with each other and use tools. We draw

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: a line in the sand and we make countries and then we create citizens and immigrants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But also ideas. I mean, the countries are centered around the concept of ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, what do you think a citizen is and an immigrant? Those are ideas. Those are ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that we impose on reality and make them real. And then they have very, very serious and real

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: effects, physical effects on people. What do you think about the idea that a bunch

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of people have written about, Dawkins with memes, which is like ideas are breeding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Like we're just like the canvas for ideas to breed in our brains. So this kind of network

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that you talk about of brains is just a little canvas for ideas to then compete against each

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: other and so on. I think as a rhetorical tool, it's cool to think that way. So I think it was

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Michael Pollan, I don't remember if it was in the Botany of Desire, but it was in one of his early

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: books on botany and gardening where he wrote about plants utilizing humans for their own

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: evolutionary purposes. But it's kind of interesting. You can think about a human gut in a sense as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: propagation device for the seeds of tomatoes and what have you. So it's kind of cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So I think rhetorically, it's an interesting device, but ideas are, as far as I know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: invented by humans, propagated by humans. So I don't think they're separate from human brains

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in any way, although it is interesting to think about it that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, of course, the ideas that are using your brain to communicate and write excellent books,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and they basically pick you, Lisa, as an effective communicator and thereby are winning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So that's an interesting worldview to think that there's particular aspects of your brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that are conducive to certain sets of ideas, and maybe those ideas will win out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, I think the way that I would say it really though is that there are many species of animals

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that influence each other's nervous systems, that regulate each other's nervous systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and they mainly do it by physical means. They do it by chemicals, scent. They do it by, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: so termites and ants and bees, for example, use chemical scents. Mammals like rodents use scent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and they also use hearing, audition, and that little bit of vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Primate, you know, non-human primates add vision, right? And I think everybody uses touch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Humans, as far as I know, are the only species that use ideas and words to regulate each other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: right? I can text something to someone halfway around the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: That's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: They don't have to hear my voice. They don't have to see my voice. They don't have to hear my voice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: They don't have to see my face, and I can have an effect on their nervous system. And ideas,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the ideas that we communicate with words, I mean, words are in a sense a way for us to do mental

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: telepathy with each other, right? I mean, I'm not the first person to say that, obviously, but how

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: do I control your heart rate? How do I control your breathing? How do I control your actions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: with words? It's because those words are communicating ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So you also write, I think, let's go back to the brain. You write that Plato gave us the idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that the human brain has three brains in it, three forces, which is kind of a compelling notion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: You disagree. First of all, what are the three parts of the brain, and why do you disagree?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So Plato's description of the psyche, which for the moment we'll just assume is the same as a mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: There are some scholars who would say a soul, a psyche, a mind, those aren't actually all the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: thing in ancient Greece, but we'll just for now gloss over that. So Plato's idea was that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and it was a description of really about moral behavior and moral responsibility in humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: so the idea was that the human psyche can be described with a metaphor of two horses

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and a charioteer. So one horse for instincts, like feeding and fighting and fleeing and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: reproduction. I'm trying to control my salty language, which apparently they print in English,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which apparently they print in England. I actually tossed off a fairly-

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: F, S?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, F, F.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. I was like, you printed that. I couldn't believe you printed that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Without the stars or whatever?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Oh, no, no, there was full print. They also printed a B word and it was really white.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: We should learn something from England.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Indeed. Anyways, but instincts, and then the other horse represents emotions and then the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: charioteer represents rationality, which controls the two beasts. Fast forward a couple of centuries

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and in the middle of the 20th century, there was a very popular view of brain evolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which suggested that you have this reptilian core, like an inner lizard brain for instincts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And then wrapped around that evolved, later on top of that evolved a limbic system in mammals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: The novelty was in a mammalian brain, which bestowed mammals with, gave them emotions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the capacity for emotions. And then on top of that evolved a cerebral cortex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which largely in primates, but very large in humans. And it's not that I personally disagree,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's that as far back as the 1960s, but really by the 1970s, it was shown pretty clearly with

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: evidence from molecular genetics, so peering into cells in the brain to look at the molecular

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: makeup of genes that the brain did not evolve that way. And the irony is that the idea of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: three layered brain with an inner lizard that hijacks your behavior and causes you to do and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: say things that you would otherwise not, or maybe that you will regret later. That idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: became very popular, was popularized by Carl Sagan in the Dragons of Eden, which won a Pulitzer prize

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in 1977, when it was already known pretty much in evolutionary neuroscience that the whole

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: narrative was a myth. So, well, the narrative is on the way it evolved, but do you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I mean, again, it's that problem of it being a useful tool of conversation to say like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: there's a lizard brain and there's a, like, if I get overly emotional on Twitter, that was the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: lizard brain and so on, but do you? No, I don't think it's useful. I think it's,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I think that- Is it useful? Is it accurate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I don't think it's accurate and therefore I don't think it's useful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So here's what I would say, you know, I think that the way I think about philosophy

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and science is that they are useful tools for living. And in order to be useful tools for living,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: they have to help you make good decisions. The trion brain, as it's called, this three layer

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain, the idea that your brain is like an already baked cake and, you know, the cerebral cortex just

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: layered on top like icing. That idea is the foundation of the law in most Western countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: It's the foundation of economic theory and it's a great narrative. It sort of fits our intuitions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: about how we work, but it also, in addition to being wrong, it lets people off the hook for

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: nasty behavior, you know? And it also suggests that emotions can't be a source of wisdom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which they often are. In fact, you would not want to be around someone who didn't have emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: That's a psychopath. I mean, that's not someone you want to really have that person deciding your

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: outcome. So I guess my, and I could sort of go on and on and on, but my point is that I don't think

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's a useful narrative in the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: What's the more accurate view of the brain that we should use when we're thinking about it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I'll answer that in a second, but I'll say that even our notion of what an instinct is or what a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: reflex is, it's not quite right. So if you look at evidence from ecology, for example, and you look

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: at animals in their ecological context, what you can see is that even things which are reflexes

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: are very context sensitive. The brains of those animals are executing so-called instinctual

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: actions in a very, very context sensitive way. And so even when a physician takes the,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's like the idea of your patellar reflex where they hit your patellar tendon on your knee and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you kick, the force with which you kick and so on is influenced by all kinds of things. A reflex

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: isn't like a robotic response. And so I think a better way is a way to think about how brains

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: work is the way that matches our best scientific understanding, which I think is really cool

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: because it's really counterintuitive. So how I came to this view, and I'm certainly not the only

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: one who holds this view, I was reading work on neuroanatomy and the view that I'm about to tell

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you was strongly suggested by that. And then I was reading work in signal processing, like by

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: electrical engineering. And similarly, the work suggested that the research suggested that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain worked this way. And I'll just say that I was reading across multiple literatures and they

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: were who don't speak to each other and they were all very, very, very, very, very, very,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: very intelligent and they were all pointing in this direction. And so far, although some of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: details are still up for grabs, the general gist, I think, is I've not come across anything yet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which really violates and I'm looking. And so the idea is something like this. It's very

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: counterintuitive. So the way to describe it is to say that your brain doesn't react to things in

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it feels like our eyes are windows on the world. We see things, we hear things, we react to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: In psychology, we call this stimulus response. So your face is your voice is a stimulus to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I receive input and then I react to it. And I might react very automatically, system one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And, but I also might execute some control where I maybe stop myself from saying something or doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: something and more in a more reflective way, execute a different action, right? That system too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: The way the brain works though, is it's predicting all the time. It's constantly talking to itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: constantly talking to your body. And it's constantly predicting what's going on in the body and what's

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: going on in the world and making predictions and the information from your body and from the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: really confirm or correct those predictions. So fundamentally the thing that the brain does

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: most of the time is just predict, like talking to itself and predicting stuff about the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: not like this dumb thing that just senses and response, senses and response.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. So the way to think about it is like this, your brain is trapped in a dark silent box.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. That's very romantic of you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Which is your skull. And the only information that it receives from your body and from the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: right? Is through the senses, through the sense organs, your eyes, your ears, and you have sensory

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: data that comes from your body that you're largely unaware of to your brain, which we call

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: interoceptive as opposed to exteroceptive, which is the world around you. But your brain is receiving

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: sense data continuously, which are the effect of some set of causes. Your brain doesn't know the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: cause of these sense data, it's only receiving the effects of those causes, which are the data

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: themselves. And so your brain has to solve what philosophers call an inverse inference problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: How do you know when you only receive the effects of something, how do you know what caused those

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: effects? So when there's a flash of light or a change in air pressure or a tug somewhere in your

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: body, how does your brain know what caused those events so that it knows what to do next to keep

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you alive and well? And the answer is that your brain has one other source of information available

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to it, which is your past experience. It can reconstitute in its wiring past experiences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and it can combine those past experiences in novel ways. And so we have lots of names for this

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in psychology. We call it memory, we call it perceptual inference, we call it simulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's also, we call it concepts or conceptual knowledge, we call it prediction. Basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: if we were to stop the world right now, stop time, your brain is in a state and it's representing

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: what it believes is going on in your body and in the world, and it's predicting what will happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in your body and in the world, and it's predicting what will happen next based on past experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: probabilistically what's most likely to happen. And it begins to prepare your action and it begins

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to prepare your experience based, so it's anticipating the sense data it's going to receive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And then when those data come in, they either confirm that prediction and your action executes

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: because the plan's already been made, or there's some sense data that your brain didn't predict

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that's unexpected and your brain takes it in, we say encodes it, we have a fancy name for that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: we call it learning. Your brain learns and it updates its storehouse of knowledge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which we call an internal model so that you can predict better next time. And it turns out that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: predicting and correcting, predicting and correcting is a much more metabolically efficient

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: way to run a system than constantly reacting all the time. Because if you're constantly reacting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it means you can't anticipate in any way what's going to happen. And so the amount of uncertainty

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that you have to deal with is overwhelming to a nervous system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Metabolically costly, I like it. And so what is a reflex? A reflex is when

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: your brain doesn't check against the sense data, that the potential cost to you is so great,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: maybe because your life is threatened, that your brain makes the prediction and executes the action

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: without checking. Yeah, so but prediction is still at the core, that's a beautiful vision of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain. I wonder, from almost an AI perspective, but just computationally, is the brain just mostly a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: prediction machine then? Like is the perception just a nice little feature added on top? Like the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: both the integration of new perceptual information. I wonder how big of an impressive

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: system is that relative to just the big predictor, model constructor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, I think that we can look to evolution for that for one answer, which is that when you go

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: back, you know, 550 million years, give or take, we, you know, the world was populated by creatures,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: really ruled by creatures without brains. And, you know, that's a biological statement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: not a political statement. You're calling dinosaurs dumb? You're talking about like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Oh, no, I'm not talking about dinosaurs, honey. I'm talking way back, further back than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Really, these, they're these little, little creatures called amphioxus, which is the modern,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's a, or a lancet, that's the modern animal. But it's an animal that scientists believe is very

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: similar to our common, the common ancestor that we share with invertebrates. Because, basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: because of the tracing back the molecular genetics in cells. And that animal had no brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: This is a hard, scientists hate this because it's a hard question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: We don't have the answer to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Have you taken a side?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I think I have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: You would have free will?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I think I have taken a side, but I don't put a lot of stock in my own intuitions or anybody's

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: intuitions about the cause of things, right? One thing we know about the brain for sure is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the brain creates experiences for us. My brain creates experiences for me, your brain creates

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: experiences for you in a way that lures you to believe that those experiences actually reveals

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the way that it works, but it doesn't. So, the-

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So, you don't trust your own intuition about free will?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Not really, not really. No, I mean, no, but I am also somewhat persuaded by, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I think Dan Dennett wrote at one point, like, you know, the philosopher Dan Dennett wrote at

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: one point that it's, I can't say it as eloquently as him, but people obviously have free will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: They are obviously making choices. So, you know, and so there is this observation

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that we're not robots and we can do some things like a little more sophisticated than an amphioxis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So, here's what I would say. I would say that your predictions, your internal model

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: attach them to ideas is based on the fact that you have years of experience knowing what these

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: didn't we? When we were- I don't know. I would have to access my memory module.

body.input: I think when I was in your- The class thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, I think we did it just like that actually. So, bravo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Wow. Yeah. I have to go look back to the tape.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. Anyways, the idea though is that your brain is using past experience and it can use past

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: experience in- so it's remembering, but you're not consciously remembering. It's basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: re-implementing prior experiences as a way of predicting what's going to happen next.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And it can do something called conceptual combination, which is it can take bits and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: pieces of the past and combine it in new ways. So, you can experience and make sense of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that you've never encountered before because you've encountered something similar to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And so, a brain in a sense is not just- doesn't just contain information,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it is information gaining, meaning it can create new information by this generative process. So,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in a sense, you could say, well, that maybe that's a source of free will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But I think really where free will comes from or the kind of free will that I think is worth

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: having a conversation about involves cultivating experiences for yourself that change your internal

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: model. When you were born and you were raised in a particular context, your brain wired itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to your surroundings, to your physical surroundings and also to your social surroundings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So, you were handed an internal model basically. But when you grow up, the more control you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: over where you are and what you do, you can cultivate new experiences for yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And those new experiences can change your internal model. And you can actually practice those

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: experiences in a way that makes them automatic, meaning it makes it easier for your brain to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: them again. And I think that that is something like what you would call free will. You aren't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: responsible for the model that you were handed, that someone, you know, your caregivers cultivated

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: a model in your brain. You're not responsible for that model, but you are responsible for the one

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you have now. You can choose, you choose what you expose yourself to. You choose how you spend your

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: time. Not everybody has choice over everything, but everybody has a little bit of choice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And so, I think that is something that I think is arguably called free will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, there's like the ripple effects of the billions of decisions you make early on in life

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: are so great that even if it's not, even if it's like all deterministic, just the amount of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: possibilities that are created and then the focusing of those possibilities into a single

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: trajectory, that somewhere within that, that's free will. Even if it's all deterministic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that might as well be just the number of choices that are possible and the fact that you just make

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: one trajectory to those set of choices seems to be like something like they'll be called free will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But it's still kind of sad to think like there doesn't seem to be a place where there's magic

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in there, where it is all just a computer. Well, there's lots of magic, I would say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: so far because we don't really understand how all of this is exactly played out at a,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I mean, scientists are working hard and disagree about some of the details under the hood of what

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I just described, but I think there's quite a bit of magic actually. And also there's also

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: there's also stochastic firing of neurons. Neurons don't, they're not purely digital in the sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that there is, there's also analog communication between neurons, not just digital. So it's not

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: just with firing of axons and some of that, there are other ways to communicate. And also

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: there's noise in the system and the noise is there for a really good reason. And that is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the more variability there is, the more potential there is for your brain to

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So you think, yeah, I guess the construction of the mental model that you use for prediction

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the story of your past. Oh boy. Yeah. That's one poetic and also just awe-inspiring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: What about the other thing you talk about? You've mentioned about sensory perception as a thing that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129
