metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: reason why we can be pretty sure that there's a there there is that the structure of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: information in the world, what we call statistical regularities in sights and sounds and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and the structure of the information that comes from your body, it's not random stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: There's a structure to it. There's a spatial structure and a temporal structure. And that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: spatial and temporal structure wires your brain. So an infant brain is not a miniature adult brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: It's a brain that is waiting for wiring instructions from the world. And it must receive

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: those wiring instructions to develop in a typical way. So for example, when a newborn is born,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: really for all your senses. So the point is that the physical world, the sense data from the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: physical world, wires your brain so that you have an internal model of that world so that your brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: can predict well to keep you alive and well and allow you to thrive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: That's fascinating that the brain is waiting for a very specific kind of set of instructions from

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the world. Not the specific, but a very specific kind of instructions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. So scientists call it expectable input. The brain needs some input in order to develop

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: normally. And we are genetically, as I say in the book, we have the kind of nature that requires

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: nurture. We can't develop normally without sensory input from the world and from the body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And what's really interesting about humans and some other animals too, but really seriously

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in humans, is the input that we need is not just physical, it's also social. In order for an infant

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to develop normally, that infant needs eye contact, touch, it needs certain types of smells,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it needs to be cuddled. So without social input, that infant's brain will not wire itself in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: neurotypical way. And again, I would say there are lots of cultural patterns of caring for an infant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: It's not like the infant has to be cared for in one way. Whatever the social environment is for an

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: infant, that it will be reflected in that infant's internal model. So we have lots of different

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: cultures, lots of different ways of rearing children, and that's an advantage. And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: we have a lot of different ways of rearing children, and that's an advantage for our species,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: although we don't always experience it that way. That is an advantage for our species. But if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: just feed and water a baby without all the extra social doodads, what you get is a profoundly

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: important thing. But nevertheless, you're kind of saying that the physical reality has a consistent

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: thing throughout that keeps feeding these set of sensory information that our brains are constructed

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: for. Yeah, the cool thing though is that if you change the consistency, if you change the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: statistical regularities, so prediction error, your brain can learn it. It's expensive for your

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain to learn it, and it takes a while for the brain to get really automated with it. But you

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: had a wonderful conversation with David Eagleman, who just published a book about this and gave

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: lots and lots of really very, very cool examples, some of which I actually discussed in how emotions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: were made, but not obviously to the extent that he did in his book. It's a fascinating book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and it speaks to the point that your internal model is always under construction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Therefore, you always can modify your experience. I wonder what the limits are. If we put it on

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Mars, or if we put it in virtual reality, or if we sit at home during a pandemic and we spend most

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of our day on Twitter and TikTok, I wonder where the breaking point, the limitations of the brain's

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: capacity to properly continue wiring itself. Well, I think what I would say is that there

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: are different ways to specify your question. One way to specify it would be the way that David

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: phrases it, which is, can we create a new sense? Can we create a new sensory modality? How hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: would that be? What are the limits in doing that? But another way to say it is, what happens to a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain when you remove some of those statistical regularities? What happens to an adult brain when

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you remove some of the statistical patterns that were there and they're not there anymore?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Are you talking about in the environment or in the actual, like, you remove eyesight, for example?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, either way. Basically, one way to limit the inputs to your brain are to stay home and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: protect yourself. Another way is to put someone in solitary confinement. Another way is to stick them

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in a nursing home. Well, not all nursing homes, but there are some, right? Which really are

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: where people are somewhat impoverished in the interactions and the variety of sensory

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: stimulation that they get. Another way is that you lose a sense, right? But the point is, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that the human brain really likes variety, to say it in a sort of Cartesian way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Variety is a good thing for a brain. And there are risks that you take when you restrict what you

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: expose yourself to. Yeah. There's all this talk of diversity. The brain loves it to the fullest

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: definition and degree of diversity. Yeah. I mean, I would say the only thing, basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: human brains thrive on diversity. The only place where we seem to have difficulty with diversity

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is with each other. Right? But who wants to eat the same food every day? You never would. Who wants

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to wear the same clothes every day? I mean, my husband, if you ask him to close his eyes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: he won't be able to tell you what he's wearing. He'll buy seven shirts of exactly the same style

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in different colors. But they are in different colors, right? It's not like he's wearing...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: How would you then explain my brain, which is terrified of choice, and therefore I wear the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: same thing every time? Well, you must be getting your diversity. Well, first of all, you are a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: fairly sharp dresser, so there is that. So you're getting some reinforcement for dressing the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that you do. But no, your brain must get diversity in other places. But I think we... So the two most

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: expensive things your brain can do, metabolically speaking, is move your body and learn something

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: new. So novelty, that is diversity, right, comes at a cost, a metabolic cost, but it's a cost,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's an investment that gives returns. And in general, people vary in how much they like

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: novelty, unexpected things. Some people really like it, some people really don't like it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and there's everybody in between. But in general, we don't eat the same thing every day. We don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: usually do exactly the same thing in exactly the same order, in exactly the same place every day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: The only place we have difficulty with diversity is in each other. And then we have considerable

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: problems there, I would say, as a species. Let me ask, I don't know if you're familiar

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: with Donald Hoffman's work about questions of reality. What are your thoughts of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: possibility that the very thing we've been talking about, of the brain wiring itself from birth to a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: particular set of inputs, is just a little slice of reality, that there is something much bigger

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: out there that we humans, with our cognition, cognitive capabilities, are just not even

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: perceiving. That the thing we're perceiving is just a crappy, like Windows 95 interface onto a much

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: bigger, richer set of complex physics that we're not even in touch with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, without getting too metaphysical about it, I think we know for sure. It doesn't have to be the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: crappy version of anything, but we definitely have a limited, we have a set of senses that are limited

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in very physical ways, and we're clearly not perceiving everything there is to perceive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: That's clear. I mean, it's just, it's not that hard. We can't, without special, why do we invent

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: scientific tools? It's so that we can overcome our senses and experience things that we couldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: otherwise, whether they are different parts of the light spectrum or things that are too

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: microscopically small for us to see or too far away for us to see. So clearly, we're only getting

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: a slice. And that slice, the interesting or potentially sad thing about humans is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: whatever we experience, we think there's a natural reason for experiencing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And we think it's obvious and natural and it must be this way, and that all the other stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: isn't important. And that's clearly not true. Many of the things that we think of as natural

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: are anything but, they're certainly real, but we've created them. They certainly have very real

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: impacts, but we've created those impacts. And we also know that there are many things outside of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that you're completely unaware of is that when your brain is basically asking itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: figuratively speaking, not literally, right? Like how is the sense, the last time I was in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: sensory array with this stuff going on in my body and I, and that this chain of events,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which just occurred, what did I do next? What did I feel next? What did I see next? And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it doesn't come up with one answer. It comes up with a distribution of it, possible answers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And then there has to be some selection process. And so you have a network in your brain, a sub

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: or not you feel in control, whether or not you feel like you're expending effort doesn't really

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to steer that internal model so that it doesn't go completely off the rails.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. Again, that wiring to the other brain, that's the guide, is at least a tiny little tether.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Exactly. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Let's talk about emotion a little bit, if we could. Emotion comes up often,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and I have never spoken with anybody who has a clarity about emotion from a biological and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: neuroscience perspective that you do. And I'm not sure I fully know how to... I mention this way too

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: much, but as somebody who was born in the Soviet Union and romanticizes basically everything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: talks about love nonstop, emotion is a... I don't know what to make of it. I don't know what...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So maybe let's just try to talk about it. From a neuroscience perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: we talked about it a little bit last time, your book covers it, how emotions are made, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: what are some misconceptions we writers of poetry, we romanticizing humans have about emotion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that we should move away from before to think about emotion from both a scientific and an

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: engineering perspective? Yeah. So there is a common view of emotion in the West. The caricature

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of that view is that we have an inner beast, right? Your delimbiac system, your inner lizard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: We have an inner beast and that comes baked in to the brain at birth. So you've got circuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: for anger, sadness, fear. It's interesting that they all have English names, these circuits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Sorry. And they're there and they're triggered by things in the world and then they cause you to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and say... So when your fear circuit is triggered, you widen your eyes, you gasp, your heart rate

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: goes up, you prepare to flee or to freeze. And these are modal responses. They're not the only

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: responses that you give, but on average, they're the prototypical responses. That's the view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And that's the view of emotion in the law. That's the view that emotions are these profoundly

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: unhelpful things that are obligatory kind of leg reflexes. The problem with that view is that it

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: doesn't comport to the evidence and it doesn't really matter. The evidence actually lines up

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: beautifully with each other. It just doesn't line up with that view. And it doesn't matter whether

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you're measuring people's faces, facial movements, or you're measuring their body movements, or you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: measuring their peripheral physiology, or you're measuring their brains or their voices or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Pick any output that you want to measure and any system you want to measure and you don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: really find strong evidence for this. And I say this as somebody who not only has reviewed really

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: thousands of articles and run big meta-analyses, which are statistical summaries of published

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: papers, but also as someone who has sent teams of researchers to small scale cultures, remote cultures,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which are very different from urban large scale cultures like ours. And one culture that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: visited, and I say we, euphemistically because I myself didn't go because I only had two research

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: permits and I gave them to my students because I felt like it was better for them to have that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: experience and more formative for them to have that experience. But I was in contact with them

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: every day by satellite phone and this was to visit the Hadza hunter-gatherers in Tanzania,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: who are not an ancient people, they're a modern culture, but they live in circumstances,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: hunting and foraging, circumstances that are very similar, in similar conditions to our ancestors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: hunting gathering ancestors, when expressions of emotion were supposed to have evolved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: at least by one view of, okay. So for many years, I was sort of struggling with this set of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: observations, right? Which is that I feel emotion and I perceive emotion in other people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: but scientists can't find a single marker, a single biomarker, not a single individual measure

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: or pattern of measures that can predict what kind of emotional state they're in. How can you

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: possibly make sense of those two things? And through a lot of reading and immersing myself

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in different literatures, I came to the hypothesis that the brain is constructing these instances

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: out of more basic ingredients. So when I tell you that the brain, when I suggest to you that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: what your brain is doing is making a prediction and it's asking itself, figuratively speaking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the last time I was in this situation and this physical state, what did I do next? What did I

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: see next? What did I hear next? It's basically asking what in my past is similar to the present.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Things which are similar to one another are called a category.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: A group of things which are similar to one another is a category. And a mental representation of a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: category is a concept. So your brain is constructing categories or concepts on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: fly continuously. So you really want to understand what a brain is doing. Using machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: like classification models is not going to help you because the brain doesn't classify,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's doing category construction. And the categories change, but the brain doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: change. Or you could say it's doing concept construction. It's using past experience to

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: conjure a concept which is a prediction. And if it's using past experiences of emotion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: then it's constructing an emotion concept. Your concept will be the content of it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and the content of it is changes depending on the situation that you're in. So for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: if your brain uses past experiences of anger that you have learned, either because somebody

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: labeled them for you, taught them to you, you observed them in movies and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in one situation could be very different from your concept of anger than another situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So now, instances of anger are what we call a population of variable instances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Sometimes when you're angry, you scowl. Sometimes when you're angry, you might smile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Sometimes when you're angry, you might cry. Sometimes your heart rate will go up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it will go down, it will stay the same. It depends on what action you're about to take.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: The idea that physiology is yoked to action is a very old idea in the study of the peripheral

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: nervous system. It's been known for really decades. And so if you look at what the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is doing, if you just look at the anatomy, here's the hypothesis that you would come up with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And I can go into the details. I've published these details in scientific papers and they also

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: appear somewhat in How Emotions Are Made, my first book. They are not in the seven and a half lessons

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: because that book is really not pitched at that level of explanation. It's really just a set of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: little essays. But what I'm about to say is actually based on scientific evidence. When your

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain begins to form a prediction, the first thing it's doing is it's making a prediction of how to

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: change the internal systems of your body, your heart, your cardiovascular system, the control of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: your heart, control of your lungs, a flush of cortisol, which is not a stress hormone,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it's a hormone that gets glucose into your bloodstream very fast because your brain is

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: predicting you need to do something metabolically expensive. And so that means either move or learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Okay? And so your brain is preparing your body, the internal systems of your body,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to execute some actions, to move in some way. And then it infers based on those motor predictions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and what we call viscera motor predictions, meaning the changes in the viscera that your

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: brain is preparing to execute. Your brain makes an inference about what you will sense based on those

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: motor movements. So your experience of the world and your experience of your own body

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: are a consequence of those predictions, those concepts. When your brain makes a concept for

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: emotion, it's constructing an instance of that emotion. That is how emotions are made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And those concepts load in, the predictions that are made include

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: contents inside the body, contents outside the body, I mean, it includes other humans. So just

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: this construction of a concept includes the variables that are much richer than just some

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: sort of simple notion. Yeah. So our colloquial notion of a concept where, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: where I say, well, what's the concept of a bird? And then you list a set of features off to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: That's people's understanding, you know, typically of what a concept is. But if you go

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: into the literature in cognitive science, what you'll see is that the way that scientists have

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: understood what a concept is has really changed over the years. So people used to think about a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: concept as philosophers and scientists used to think about a concept as a dictionary definition

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: for a category. So there's a set of things which are similar out in the world. And your concept

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: your concept for that category is a dictionary definition of the features, the necessary and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: sufficient features of that, of those instances. So for a bird, you know, it would be wings, feathers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: right? A beak, it flies, whatever. Okay. That's called the classical category.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And scientists discovered, observed that actually not all instances of birds have feathers and not

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: all instances of birds fly. And so the idea was that you don't have a single representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of necessary and sufficient features stored in your brain somewhere. Instead, what you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is a prototype, a prototype meaning you still have a single representation for the category one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: but the features are like of the most typical instance of the category or maybe the most

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: frequent instance, but not all instances of the category have all the features, right? They have

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: some graded similarity to the prototype. And then, you know, what I'm going to like incredibly

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: simplify now a lot of work to say that then a series of experiments were done to show that in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: what your brain seems to be doing is coming up with a single exemplar or instance of the category

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and reading off the features when I ask you for the concept. So if we were in a pet store,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and I asked you what are the features of a bird, tell me the concept of bird, you would be more

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: likely to give me features of a good pet. And if we were in a restaurant, you would be more likely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you know, like a budgie, right? Or a canary. If we were in a restaurant, you would be more likely

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to give me the features of a bird that you would eat, like a chicken. And if we were in a park,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you'd be more likely to give me in this country, you know, the features of a sparrow or a robin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Whereas if we were in South America, you would probably give me the features of a peacock,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: because that's more common, or it is more common there than here that you would see a peacock in

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: such circumstances. So the idea was that really what your brain was doing was conjuring a concept

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: on the fly that meets the function that the category is being put to. Okay? Okay. Then

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: people started studying ad hoc concepts, meaning concepts that where the instances don't share

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: any physical features, but the function of the instances are the same. So for example, think

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: about all the things that can protect you from the rain. What are all the things that can protect

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you from the rain? Umbrella, like this apartment. Right. Your car. Not giving a damn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Like a mindset. Yeah, right. Right. So the idea is that the function of the instances is the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in a given situation, even if they look different, sound different, smell different. This is called

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: an abstract concept or a conceptual concept. Now, the really cool thing about conceptual concepts

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: or conceptual categories is a category of things that are held together by a function, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: called an abstract concept or a conceptual category, because the things don't share

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: physical features, they share functional features. There are two really cool things about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: One is that's what Darwin said a species was. Darwin is known for discovering natural selection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: but the other thing he really did, which was really profound, which he's less celebrated for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is understanding that all biological categories have inherent variation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Inherent variation. Darwin wrote in The Origin of Species about, before Darwin's book, a species was

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: thought to be a classical category, where all the instances of dogs were the same, had exactly same

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: features, and any variation from that perfect platonic instance was considered to be error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And Darwin said, no, it's not error, it's meaningful. Nature selects on the basis of that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: variation. The reason why natural selection is powerful and can exist is because there is

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: variation in a species. And in dogs, we talk about that variation in terms of the size of the dog and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the amount of fur the dog has and the color and how long is the tail and how long is the snout.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: In humans, we talk about that variation in all kinds of ways, including in cultural ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So that's one thing that's really interesting about conceptual categories is that Darwin

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: is basically saying a species is a conceptual category. And in fact, if you look at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: modern debates about what is a species, you can't find anybody agreeing on what the criteria are

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: for a species because they don't all share the same genome. We don't all share, there isn't a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: single human genome. There's a population of genomes, but they're variable. It's not

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: unbounded variation, but they are variable. And the other thing that's really cool about conceptual

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: categories is that they are the categories that we use to make civilization. So think about money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: for example. What are all the physical things that make something a currency? Is there any

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: physical feature that all the currencies in all the worlds that's ever been used by humans share?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Well, certainly, right. But what is it? Is it definable? So it's getting to the point that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: make it as function. It's the function. It's that we trade it for material goods. And we have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: agree. We all impose on whatever it is, salt, barley, little shelves, big rocks in the ocean

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that can't move, Bitcoin, pieces of plastic, mortgages, which are basically a promise of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: something in the future, nothing more. All of these things, we impose value on them. And we all

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: agree that we can exchange them for material goods. By the way, you're attributing some of that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to Darwin that he thought... No, I'm saying that what Darwin...

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Because it's a brilliant view of what a species is, is the function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. What I'm saying is that what Darwin really talked about variation in... So if you read, for

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: example, the biologist Ernst Mayr, who was an evolutionary biologist, and then when he retired,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: became a historian and philosopher of biology. And his suggestion is that Darwin did talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: variation. He vanquished what's called essentialism, the idea that there's a single

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: set of features that define any species. And out of that grew

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: really discussions of some of the functional features that species have, like they can reproduce,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: they can have offspring, the individuals of a species can have offspring. It turns out

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that's not a perfect criterion to use, but it's a functional criterion. So what I'm saying is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in cognitive science, people came up with the idea, they discovered the idea of conceptual

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: categories or ad hoc concepts, these concepts that can change based on the function they're serving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: It's in Darwin and it's also in the philosophy of social reality. The way that philosophers talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: about social reality, just look around you. We're treating a bunch of things as similar,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which are physically different, but we're treating them in a way that's not just a

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: bunch of things as similar, which are physically different. And sometimes we take things that are

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: physically the same and we treat them as separate categories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But it feels like the number of variables involved in that kind of categorization is nearly infinite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: No, I don't think so because there is a physical constraint, right? Like you and I could agree

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that we can fly in real life, but we can't. That's a physical constraint that we can't break.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: You and I could agree that we could walk through the walls, but we can't. We could agree that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: could eat glass. Oh, there's a lot of constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, we could agree that the virus doesn't exist and we don't have to wear masks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But physical reality still holds the trump card, right? But still there's a lot of-

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: The trump card, well, pun unintended.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Pun completely unintended, but there you go. That's a predicting brain for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: But there's a tremendous amount of leeway. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah, that's the point. So what I'm saying is that emotions are like money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Basically, they're like money. They're like countries. They're like kings and queens and

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: presidents. They're like everything that we construct, that we impose meaning on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: We take these physical signals and we give them meanings that they don't otherwise have by their

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: physical nature. And because we agree, they have that function. But the beautiful thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: so maybe I'm like money, I love this similarity is it's not obvious to me that this kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: emergent agreement should happen with emotion because our experiences are so different for each

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of us humans and yet we kind of converge. Well, in a culture we converge, but not across

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: cultures. There are huge, huge differences. There are huge differences in what concepts exist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: what they look like. So what I would say is that-

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: They feel like- What we're doing with our young children as their brains become wired to their

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: physical and their social environment is that we are curating for them. We are bootstrapping into

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: their brains a set of emotion concepts. That's partly what they're learning. And we curate those

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: for infants just the way we curate for them what is a dog, what is a cat, what is a truck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: We sometimes explicitly label and we sometimes just use mental words. When your kid is throwing

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Cheerios on the floor instead of eating them or your kid is crying when she won't put herself

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to sleep or whatever. We use mental words and for infants words are these really special things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that they help infants learn abstract categories. There's a huge literature showing that children

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: can take things that don't look infants, like infants, really young infants, pre-verbal infants

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: can take, if you label, if I say to you and you're an infant, okay, so I say, Lex, Lexie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: this is a bling. And I put it down and the bling makes a squeaky noise. And then I say, Lexie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: I'm getting excited by the way. This is a bling. And I put it down and it makes a squeaky noise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: And then I say, Lexie, this is a bling. You, as young as four months old, will expect

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: this to make a noise. Yeah. A squeaky noise. And if you don't, if it doesn't, you'll be surprised

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: because it violated your expectation, right? I'm building for you an internal model of a bling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Okay. Infants can do this really, really at a young age. And so there's no reason to believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that they couldn't learn emotion categories and concepts in the same way. And in one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and what happens when you go to a new culture? When you go to a new culture,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you have to do what's called emotion acculturation. So my colleague, Batia Mesquita,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: in Belgium studies emotion acculturation. She studies how when people move from one culture

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: to another, how do they learn the emotion concepts of that culture? How do they learn to make sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of their own internal sensations and also the movements, you know, the rays of an eyebrow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: the tilt of a head, how do they learn to make sense of cues from other people using emotions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: using concepts they don't have, but have to make on the fly?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So that's the difference in cultures. Let me open another door. I'm not sure I want to open,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: but difference between men and women. Is there a difference between the emotional lives

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: of those two categories of biological systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So here's what I would say. You know, we did a series of studies in the 1990s where we asked men

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and women to tell us about their emotional lives. And women described themselves as much more

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: emotional than men. They believed that they were more emotional than men and men agreed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Women are much more emotional than men. Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Okay. And then we gave them little handheld computers. These were little Hewlett Packard

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: computers. They fit in the palm of your hand. They weighed a couple of pounds. So this was like

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: pre-palm pilot even. This was, you know, 1990s and like early. And we asked them, we would,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you know, ping them like 10 times a day and just ask them to report how they were feeling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: which is called experience sampling. So we experienced sampled. And then at the end,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: and then we looked at their reports and what we found is that men and women basically didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: differ. And there were some people who were really had many more instances of emotion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: So they were, you know, they were treading water in a tumultuous sea of emotion. And then there were

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: other people who were like floating tranquilly, you know, in a lake. It was really not perturbed

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: very often and everyone in between, but there were no difference between men and women. And the really

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: interesting thing is at the end of the sampling period, we asked people, so reflect over the past

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: two weeks and tell it, so, you know, we've been now pinging people like again and again and again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: right? So tell us how emotional do you think you are? No change from the beginning. So men and women

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: believe that they are, they believe that they are different. And when they are looking at other

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: people, they make different inferences about emotion. If a man, if a man is scowling, like if

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: you and I were together and some, so somebody's watching this, okay. And yeah, hey, who was I

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: saying? Hey, hi, hi. By the way, people love it when you look at the camera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: If you and I make exactly the same set of facial movements,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: when people look at you, both men and women look at you, they are more likely to think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: oh, he's reacting to the situation. And when they look at me, they'll say, oh, she's having an

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: emotion. She's, you know, yeah. And I wrote about this actually right before the 2016 election.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: You know what, maybe I could confess. Let me try to carefully confess. But you are really going to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: Yeah. That when I, that there is an element when I see Hillary Clinton,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: that there was something annoying about her to me. And I just, that feeling, and then I tried to

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: reduce that to what, what is that? Because I think the same attributes that are annoying about her,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: when I see in other people wouldn't be annoying. So I was trying to understand what is it? Because

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129

body.input: it certainly does feel like that concept that I've constructed in my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lisa Feldman Barrett: Counterintuitive Ideas About How the Brain Works | Lex Fridman Podcast #129
